3.51.s:
3.251
haṃsa uvāca ..
anṛtaṃ varjayennityamanṛtaṃ pātakaṃ param ..
anṛtāddhi paraṃ nāsti dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ .. 1 ..
3.51.d:
3.251
हंस उवाच ॥
अनृतं वर्जयेन्नित्यमनृतं पातकं परम् ॥
अनृताद्धि परं नास्ति द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ॥ 1 ॥
3.51.m:
3.251
Haṃsa said:
One should always avoid untruth; untruth is the highest sin; / for there is no door to one's own ruin greater than untruth.

3.51.s:
sarve nibaddhā vācyārthā vāṅmūlā vāgvinissṛtāḥ..
tasmānna stenayedvācaṃ ya iccheddhitamātmanaḥ .. 2 ..
3.51.d:
सर्वे निबद्धा वाच्यार्था वाङ्मूला वाग्विनिस्सृताः॥
तस्मान्न स्तेनयेद्वाचं य इच्छेद्धितमात्मनः ॥ 2 ॥
3.51.m: All expressed meanings are bound [in speech], rooted in speech, and proceed from speech; / therefore, one who desires one's own welfare should not be a thief of speech.

3.51.s:
anṛtaṃ na kvacidvācyaṃ tathā sākṣye viśeṣataḥ ..
anṛtaṃ hi vadansākṣye pitṛbhiḥ saha majjati .. 3 ..
3.51.d:
अनृतं न क्वचिद्वाच्यं तथा साक्ष्ये विशेषतः ॥
अनृतं हि वदन्साक्ष्ये पितृभिः सह मज्जति ॥ 3 ॥
3.51.m: Untruth must never be spoken anywhere, and especially in testimony; / for speaking untruth in testimony, one sinks [into hell] together with one's ancestors.

3.51.s:
pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte ..
śatamaśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte .. 4 ..
3.51.d:
पञ्च पश्वनृते हन्ति दश हन्ति गवानृते ॥
शतमश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं पुरुषानृते ॥ 4 ॥
3.51.m: One kills five by untruth concerning cattle; one kills ten by untruth concerning kine; / one kills a hundred by untruth concerning horses; one kills a thousand by untruth concerning a human.

3.51.s:
hanti jātānajātām̐śca hiraṇyārthe'nṛtaṃ vadan ..
sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛtaṃ hanti māsma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadet .. 5 ..
3.51.d:
हन्ति जातानजाताम्̐श्च हिरण्यार्थेऽनृतं वदन् ॥
सर्वं भूम्यनृतं हन्ति मास्म भूम्यनृतं वदेत् ॥ 5 ॥
3.51.m: One kills both the born and the unborn when speaking untruth for the sake of gold; / one kills everything by untruth concerning land; one should never speak untruth concerning land.

3.51.s:
apsu bhūmivadityāhuḥ strīṇāṃ bhoge ca maithune ..
abjeṣu caiva ratneṣu sarveṣvaśmamayeṣu ca .. 6 ..
3.51.d:
अप्सु भूमिवदित्याहुः स्त्रीणां भोगे च मैथुने ॥
अब्जेषु चैव रत्नेषु सर्वेष्वश्ममयेषु च ॥ 6 ॥
3.51.m: They say that concerning water it is like land, and also in the enjoyment of women and sexual intercourse, / and concerning water-born gems and all things made of stone.

3.51.s:
etāndoṣānavekṣyaiva sarvānanṛtabhāṣaṇe ..
yathāśrutaṃ yathādṛṣṭaṃ sarvamevāñjasā vadet .. 7 ..
3.51.d:
एतान्दोषानवेक्ष्यैव सर्वाननृतभाषणे ॥
यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं सर्वमेवाञ्जसा वदेत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.51.m: Having observed all these faults in speaking untruth, / one should speak everything straightforwardly, just as heard and just as seen.

3.51.s:
nagno muṇḍaḥ kapālī ca bhikṣārthī kṣutpipāsitaḥ ..
andhaḥ śatrugṛhaṃ gacchenna sākṣyamanṛtaṃ vadet .. 8 ..
3.51.d:
नग्नो मुण्डः कपाली च भिक्षार्थी क्षुत्पिपासितः ॥
अन्धः शत्रुगृहं गच्छेन्न साक्ष्यमनृतं वदेत् ॥ 8 ॥
3.51.m: Naked, shaven-headed, carrying a skull-bowl, seeking alms, hungry and thirsty, / blind, he would go to the house of an enemy; [so] let him not speak false testimony.

3.51.s:
sākṣye'nṛtaṃ vadanpāśairbadhyate vāruṇairbhṛśam ..
niviśante tamājātīstasmātsākṣye vadedṛtam .. 9 ..
3.51.d:
साक्ष्येऽनृतं वदन्पाशैर्बध्यते वारुणैर्भृशम् ॥
निविशन्ते तमाजातीस्तस्मात्साक्ष्ये वदेदृतम् ॥ 9 ॥
3.51.m: Speaking untruth in testimony, one is bound tightly with the nooses of Varuṇa; / darknesses enter him for births; therefore, one should speak truth in testimony.

3.51.s:
yanmayā gaditaṃ pāpaṃ dvijena kūṭasākṣiṇaḥ ..
tato'dhikamavāpnoni sadyo mithyā'bhiśaṃsane .. 3.251.10 ..
3.51.d:
यन्मया गदितं पापं द्विजेन कूटसाक्षिणः ॥
ततोऽधिकमवाप्नोनि सद्यो मिथ्याऽभिशंसने ॥ 3.251.10 ॥
3.51.m: Whatever sin has been spoken of by me for a false witness, O twice-born, / more than that does he attain immediately in making a false accusation.

3.51.s:
yathā krodhādbhayāllobhādajñānādvā dvijottamāḥ ..
yo'nṛtaṃ bhāṣate sadbhyaḥ sa yāti narakaṃ dhruvam .. 11 ..
3.51.d:
यथा क्रोधाद्भयाल्लोभादज्ञानाद्वा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
योऽनृतं भाषते सद्भ्यः स याति नरकं ध्रुवम् ॥ 11 ॥
3.51.m: Whoever speaks untruth to the virtuous out of anger, fear, greed, / or ignorance, O best of twice-born, he surely goes to hell.

3.51.s:
avākchirāstamasyandhe kilbiṣī narake patet ..
yaḥ praśnaṃ vitathaṃ brūyātpṛṣṭaḥ saddharmaniścaye .. 12 ..
3.51.d:
अवाक्छिरास्तमस्यन्धे किल्बिषी नरके पतेत् ॥
यः प्रश्नं वितथं ब्रूयात्पृष्टः सद्धर्मनिश्चये ॥ 12 ॥
3.51.m: Head downwards into blind darkness the sinner would fall into hell, / who, when questioned in the determination of true dharma, gives a false answer.

3.51.s:
andho matsyānivāśnāti nirapekṣaṃ sakaṇṭakān ..
yo bhāṣate'rtha vaikalyamapratyakṣaṃ sabhāṅgataḥ ..13..
3.51.d:
अन्धो मत्स्यानिवाश्नाति निरपेक्षं सकण्टकान् ॥
यो भाषतेऽर्थ वैकल्यमप्रत्यक्षं सभाङ्गतः ॥13॥
3.51.m: As a blind man heedlessly eats fish along with the bones, / so does he who, having entered the assembly, speaks of an impairment of matter that was not directly perceived.

3.51.s:
kūṭakarmatulāmāne rasānāṃ bhedane tathā ..
viśvāsanyāsaharaṇe rahasyasamabhedane .. 14 ..
3.51.d:
कूटकर्मतुलामाने रसानां भेदने तथा ॥
विश्वासन्यासहरणे रहस्यसमभेदने ॥ 14 ॥
3.51.m: In fraudulent deeds with scales and measures, and likewise in the adulteration of liquids, / in the misappropriation of a deposit given in trust, and in the breach of a secret agreement,

3.51.s:
mṛtiṃ kalpayate yaśca madhu māṃsena pātakam ..
dvijasya surayā vāpi lobhena ca viśeṣataḥ .. 15 ..
3.51.d:
मृतिं कल्पयते यश्च मधु मांसेन पातकम् ॥
द्विजस्य सुरया वापि लोभेन च विशेषतः ॥ 15 ॥
3.51.m: And who brings about death, the sin [caused] by honey with meat, / or by wine for a twice-born, and especially out of greed;

3.51.s:
gobrāhmaṇavadhe vāpi gurupitṛvadhe tathā ..
vayasyadāragamane gurudārapradarśane .. 16 ..
3.51.d:
गोब्राह्मणवधे वापि गुरुपितृवधे तथा ॥
वयस्यदारगमने गुरुदारप्रदर्शने ॥ 16 ॥
3.51.m: or in the killing of a cow or a brahmin, and likewise in the killing of a guru or a father, / in having intercourse with a friend's wife, in exposing the guru's wife;

3.51.s:
vyutpādane ca śastrāṇāṃ śastrotsāde tathaiva ca ..
bhartṛpiṇḍāpaharaṇe saṃgrāmācca palāyane ..17..
3.51.d:
व्युत्पादने च शस्त्राणां शस्त्रोत्सादे तथैव च ॥
भर्तृपिण्डापहरणे संग्रामाच्च पलायने ॥17॥
3.51.m: and in the manufacture of weapons, and likewise in destroying weapons, / in embezzling the master's livelihood, and in fleeing from battle;

3.51.s:
śaraṇāgatasaṃtyāge gacchataśca divā striyam ..
preṣyāṃ ca gacchataḥ pāpaṃ rājadrohe tathaiva ca .. 18 ..
3.51.d:
शरणागतसंत्यागे गच्छतश्च दिवा स्त्रियम् ॥
प्रेष्यां च गच्छतः पापं राजद्रोहे तथैव च ॥ 18 ॥
3.51.m: in abandoning one who has sought refuge, and of one who approaches a woman by day, / and the sin of one who approaches a maidservant, and likewise in treason against the king;

3.51.s:
paṅktyāṃ viṣamadātuśca śrāddhaṃ mitrasya yattathā ..
śulkena dadataḥ kanyāṃ keśavikrayikasya ca .. 19 ..
3.51.d:
पङ्क्त्यां विषमदातुश्च श्राद्धं मित्रस्य यत्तथा ॥
शुल्केन ददतः कन्यां केशविक्रयिकस्य च ॥ 19 ॥
3.51.m: and of one who distributes unevenly in an assembly [of eaters], and in a śrāddha [performed] for a friend, / of one who gives away a maiden for a bride-price, and of a seller of hair;

3.51.s:
viprasya pātakaṃ yacca prāṇināṃ vikraye bhavet ..
āmaśrāddhabhujaḥ pāpamayājyasya ca yājane .. 3.251.20 ..
3.51.d:
विप्रस्य पातकं यच्च प्राणिनां विक्रये भवेत् ॥
आमश्राद्धभुजः पापमयाज्यस्य च याजने ॥ 3.251.20 ॥
3.51.m: and the sin of a brahmin that arises in the sale of living beings, / the sin of eating an āmaśrāddha, and in officiating at a sacrifice for one not entitled to sacrifice;

3.51.s:
mithyā rājyasya karaṇe paradravyāpahāriṇaḥ ..
sarvāṇyetāni pāpāni dvijaḥ sabhyaḥ samāpnuyāt .. 21 ..
3.51.d:
मिथ्या राज्यस्य करणे परद्रव्यापहारिणः ॥
सर्वाण्येतानि पापानि द्विजः सभ्यः समाप्नुयात् ॥ 21 ॥
3.51.m: in falsely ruling a kingdom, and of one who steals another's property— / all these sins a twice-born assessor in the court incurs

3.51.s:
yadyanyathā vadettasmāddharmyaṃ sabhyaḥ sadā vadet ..
etadeva tathā pāpaṃ vijñeyaṃ kūṭasākṣiṇām .. 22 ..
3.51.d:
यद्यन्यथा वदेत्तस्माद्धर्म्यं सभ्यः सदा वदेत् ॥
एतदेव तथा पापं विज्ञेयं कूटसाक्षिणाम् ॥ 22 ॥
3.51.m: if he should speak otherwise. Therefore, an assessor must always speak what is righteous. / This very same sin is to be known as belonging to false witnesses.

3.51.s:
kūṭakarmā tu narakaṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha majjati ..
daśavarṣasahasrāṇi daśavarṣaśatāni ca ..23..
3.51.d:
कूटकर्मा तु नरकं पितृभिः सह मज्जति ॥
दशवर्षसहस्राणि दशवर्षशतानि च ॥23॥
3.51.m: One who commits fraudulent deeds sinks into hell along with his ancestors / for ten thousand and ten hundred years.

3.51.s:
tato daśaguṇaṃ kālaṃ sabhyo mithyābhibhāṣitā ..
rāgadveṣapravṛttastu vyavahāre'pi pārthivaḥ .. 24 ..
3.51.d:
ततो दशगुणं कालं सभ्यो मिथ्याभिभाषिता ॥
रागद्वेषप्रवृत्तस्तु व्यवहारेऽपि पार्थिवः ॥ 24 ॥
3.51.m: An assessor who speaks falsely [dwells there] for ten times that duration; / and an earthly ruler who acts out of passion and malice in judicial proceedings

3.51.s:
tato daśaguṇaṃ kālaṃ narake vasati dhruvam ..
ukte vacasi dharmye tu sadyaḥ pāpātpramucyate .. 25 ..
3.51.d:
ततो दशगुणं कालं नरके वसति ध्रुवम् ॥
उक्ते वचसि धर्म्ये तु सद्यः पापात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 25 ॥
3.51.m: surely dwells in hell for ten times that duration. / But when righteous speech is uttered, one is instantly freed from sin.

3.51.s:
rājā narakamāpnoti satyavākyaṃ vilaṃghayana ..
śūdraviṭkṣatraviprāṇāṃ yatrokte prāpnuyādvadhaḥ .. 26 ..
3.51.d:
राजा नरकमाप्नोति सत्यवाक्यं विलंघयन ॥
शूद्रविट्क्षत्रविप्राणां यत्रोक्ते प्राप्नुयाद्वधः ॥ 26 ॥
3.51.m: A king reaches hell by transgressing truthful speech. / Where the slaughter of a śūdra, a vaiśya, a kṣatriya, or a brahmin would occur if spoken,

3.51.s:
tatra vaktavyamanṛtaṃ taddhi satyādviśiṣyate ..
vāgdaivataiśca carubhiryajanaiśca sarasvatīm ...27..
3.51.d:
तत्र वक्तव्यमनृतं तद्धि सत्याद्विशिष्यते ॥
वाग्दैवतैश्च चरुभिर्यजनैश्च सरस्वतीम् ॥.27॥
3.51.m: untruth should be spoken there, for that is superior to truth. / And with caru offerings sacred to the deity of Speech, and with sacrifices to Sarasvatī,

3.51.s:
kūṣmāṇḍairvāpi juhuyādghṛtamagnau yathāvidhi ..
udutyṛce vā vāruṇye ṛcā vāgdaivatena vā ..28..
3.51.d:
कूष्माण्डैर्वापि जुहुयाद्घृतमग्नौ यथाविधि ॥
उदुत्यृचे वा वारुण्ये ऋचा वाग्दैवतेन वा ॥28॥
3.51.m: or with the kūṣmāṇḍa [hymns], he should offer clarified butter into the fire according to rule, / or with the verse 'Udu tyaṃ' or with a Vāruṇa verse, or with a verse dedicated to the deity of Speech,

3.51.s:
anṛtasya vaśastasya kurvāṇo niṣkṛtiṃ parām..
bahavaḥ sukhamedhante yasminviprā nipātite ..
vācyaṃ tasya vadhe prāpte yathābhūtamiti śrutiḥ .. 29 ..
3.51.d:
अनृतस्य वशस्तस्य कुर्वाणो निष्कृतिं पराम्॥
बहवः सुखमेधन्ते यस्मिन्विप्रा निपातिते ॥
वाच्यं तस्य वधे प्राप्ते यथाभूतमिति श्रुतिः ॥ 29 ॥
3.51.m: falling under the power of that untruth, performing supreme expiation. / When the killing of someone has approached through whose falling many brahmins prosper happily, / what really happened should be spoken: such is the Vedic teaching.

3.51.s:
na narmayuktaṃ vacanaṃ hinasti na strīṣu viprā na vivāhakāle ..
prāṇātyaye sarvadhanāpahāre pañcānṛtānyāhurapātakāni .. 3.251.30 ..
3.252
haṃsa uvāca ..
sarveṣāmeva pāpānāṃ hiṃsā paramihocyate ..
hiṃsā balamasādhūnāṃ hiṃsā lokadvayāpahā .. 1 ..
api kīṭaḥ pataṅgo vā na hantavyaḥ kathañcana ..
mahadduḥkhamavāpnoti puruṣaḥ prāṇināśanāt .. 2 ..
ātatāyinamāyāntaṃ puruṣaṃ yadi vā paśum ..
upāyahīnastaṃ hatvā na tu pāpena bādhyate .. 3 ..
guruṃ vā bālavṛddhau vā mānyaṃ vāpyatha vā janam ..
ātatāyinamāyāntaṃ hanyādevāvicārayan .. 4 ..
ātatāyina māyāntamapi vedāntagaṃ raṇe ..
jighāṃsantaṃ jighāṃsīyāttena pāpaṃ na vidyate .. 5 ..
raṇe prahārābhihate śatrau naivāsti pātakam ..
jitvā gṛhīte nihate tasminnevāsti pātakam .. 6 ..
3.51.d:
न नर्मयुक्तं वचनं हिनस्ति न स्त्रीषु विप्रा न विवाहकाले ॥
प्राणात्यये सर्वधनापहारे पञ्चानृतान्याहुरपातकानि ॥ 3.251.30 ॥
3.252
हंस उवाच ॥
सर्वेषामेव पापानां हिंसा परमिहोच्यते ॥
हिंसा बलमसाधूनां हिंसा लोकद्वयापहा ॥ 1 ॥
अपि कीटः पतङ्गो वा न हन्तव्यः कथञ्चन ॥
महद्दुःखमवाप्नोति पुरुषः प्राणिनाशनात् ॥ 2 ॥
आततायिनमायान्तं पुरुषं यदि वा पशुम् ॥
उपायहीनस्तं हत्वा न तु पापेन बाध्यते ॥ 3 ॥
गुरुं वा बालवृद्धौ वा मान्यं वाप्यथ वा जनम् ॥
आततायिनमायान्तं हन्यादेवाविचारयन् ॥ 4 ॥
आततायिन मायान्तमपि वेदान्तगं रणे ॥
जिघांसन्तं जिघांसीयात्तेन पापं न विद्यते ॥ 5 ॥
रणे प्रहाराभिहते शत्रौ नैवास्ति पातकम् ॥
जित्वा गृहीते निहते तस्मिन्नेवास्ति पातकम् ॥ 6 ॥
3.51.m:
A statement made in jest does not harm, nor among women, O brahmins, nor at the time of marriage, / nor when life is in peril, nor at the loss of all one's wealth: they declare these five untruths to be without sin.
3.252
Haṃsa said:
Violence is declared here to be the foremost of all sins; / violence is the strength of the wicked; violence destroys both worlds.
Not even a worm or a moth should be killed in any way. / A man incurs great suffering from destroying living beings.
When an assailant attacks, whether a man or an animal, / if one devoid of [other] means kills him, he is not afflicted by sin.
Whether a guru, a child, an old man, or a venerable person, / one should slay an approaching assailant without hesitation.
Even if an approaching assailant has mastered the Vedānta, in battle / one seeking to kill should be killed; no sin is found thereby.
When an enemy is struck down by blows in battle, there is no sin at all; / there is sin only when he is killed after having been conquered and captured.

3.51.s:
raṇe jitantu yaḥ śaktaḥ paścātpātayate naraḥ ..
sa yāti narakaṃ ghoraṃ bahūnyabdaśatāni ca .. 7 ..
muktaśca nārakādduḥkhādbahūnyabdaśatāni tu ..
āmagarbheṣu sicyante ye narā naraghātakāḥ .. 8 ..

वृथापशुघ्नः प्राप्नोति प्रेत्य चेह च निष्कृतिम् ॥ 9 ॥

3.51.m:
A capable man who strikes down one already conquered in battle / goes to a dreadful hell for many hundreds of years.
And released from infernal suffering for many hundreds of years, / those men who are slayers of men are cast into unformed embryos.
As many hairs as an animal has, that many times does the slayer of an animal for no ritual purpose / suffer killing in this world, in the hereafter, and [attains no] expiation.
Even by killing an insect or cutting grass, / a man goes to hell, O knowers of dharma, through his own action.
Violence toward women, violence toward wealth, and dreadful violence toward living beings: / threefold is violence declared, shunned by wise men.
One devoted to non-violence must diligently shun another's wife, / and likewise, with great effort, another's property left even in an uninhabited place.
Therefore, terrifying violence toward living beings should not be committed at all; / the pitiless person who separates even a single living being from its life,

नरकाद्धि विनिर्मुक्तो न किञ्चित्सुखमेधते ॥
यां रात्रिमधिविन्नां स्त्रीं यां चैवाक्षपराजिताम् ॥ 14 ॥
यां च राज्यच्युतो रात्रिं यां च सर्वस्वविच्युतः ॥
इष्टबन्धुवियुक्तश्च यां रात्रिं दुःखमश्नुते ॥ 15 ॥
व्यवहारे जितश्चैव यद् दुःखं कूटसाक्षिभिः ॥
तत्सर्वं दुःखमाप्नोति हत्वैकमपि तु द्विजाः ॥ 16 ॥
नास्ति पापतरं लोके मनुष्या मांसभोजिनः॥
बहिर्मांसं तृणात्काष्ठादुपलाद्वापि जायते॥17॥
घोरात्प्राणिवधाज्जातं पुरुषः परिवर्जयेत् ॥
यदि चेत्खादको न स्यान्न भवेद्घातकस्तथा ॥ 18 ॥
एतस्मात्कारणान्निन्द्यो घातकादपि खादकः ॥।
यावतां प्राणिनां येन मांसं भुक्तं भवेदिह ॥ 19 ॥
ता एव ते न तावत्यो गन्तव्या योनयो ध्रुवम् ॥
येषान्तु प्राणिनां भुक्तं तेन मांसं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 3.252.20 ॥
3.51.m:
even when released from hell, thrives in no happiness whatsoever. / That night which a superseded wife [endures], that which one defeated at dice [suffers],
and the night one fallen from kingship [endures], that which one deprived of all possessions [suffers], / and the night one separated from beloved kinsmen experiences grief,
and that grief of one defeated in a lawsuit by false witnesses— / all that grief he incurs by killing even a single [creature], O twice-born.
There is nothing more sinful in the world, O men, than eating meat. / Meat does not arise externally from grass, wood, or stone.
A man should avoid what is born from the terrible slaughter of living beings; / if there were no eater, there would be no slayer.
For this reason, the eater is more blameworthy than even the slayer. / For as many living beings whose meat was eaten by him here,
surely that many wombs must be entered by him; / those living beings whose meat was eaten by him, O best of the twice-born,

एतन्मांसस्य मांसत्वं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥
समुत्पत्तिं च मांसस्य वधबन्धौ च देहिनाम् ॥ ॥ 22 ॥
प्रसमीक्ष्य निवर्त्येत सर्वमांसस्य भक्षणात् ॥
अनुमन्ता विशसिता निहन्ता क्रियविक्रयी ॥ 23 ॥
संस्कर्ता चोपहर्ता च खादकाश्च विघातकाः ॥
स्वमांसं परमांसेन यो वर्धयितुमिच्छति ॥ 24 ॥
न पापकृत्तमो लोके तस्मादन्यो हि विद्यते ॥
असंस्कृतान्पशून्मन्त्रैर्नाद्याद्विप्रः कथञ्चन ॥ 25 ॥
मन्त्रैस्तु संस्कृतानद्याच्छाश्वतं विधिमास्थितः ॥
या वेदविहिता हिंसा न सा हिंसा मता यतः ॥ 25 ॥
ओषध्यः पशवो वृक्षास्तिर्यञ्चः पक्षिणस्तथा ॥
यज्ञार्थं निधनं प्राप्ता प्राप्नुवन्त्युच्छ्रिताः पुनः ॥ 27 ॥
3.51.m:
his meat will surely be eaten by them birth after birth: / 'Me he will eat in the other world, whose meat I eat here'—
this the wise declare to be the essence of meat (māṃsatva). / Having observed the origin of meat and the slaughter and confinement of embodied beings,
one should refrain from eating all meat. / The consenter, the carver, the killer, the buyer and seller,
the preparer, the server, and the eaters are all slayers. / He who desires to augment his own flesh with the flesh of another—
no greater sinner than him exists in the world. / A brahmin must never eat animals that are unconsecrated by mantras.
Relying on the eternal rule, he may eat those consecrated with mantras, / since violence enjoined by the Veda is considered not to be violence.
Plants, cattle, trees, animals, and likewise birds, / having met their end for the purpose of sacrifice, attain an exalted state again.

3.51.m:
At the madhuparka offering, in sacrifice, and in rites for ancestors and deities— / only in these may animals be killed, and never elsewhere.
Twice-born men who understand the true meaning of the Veda and kill beasts for these purposes, / lead both themselves and the beasts to the highest state.
Animals were created by the Self-born at the very beginning for the purpose of sacrifice, / and sacrifices [are ordained] for the well-being of all; therefore, killing in sacrifice is not killing.

॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
पापं कृत्वा नरो विप्रा नरकं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
नरकाच्च विनिर्मुक्तस्तिर्यग्योनौ तथा व्रजेत् ॥ 2॥

3.51.m:
A man who eats meat in vain, O brahmins, goes to a dreadful hell. / Slashing the life of a creature is utterly censured, and for that reason meat should be avoided.
3.253
The sages said:
Tell us, O best of the twice-born, knower of dharma, king of birds, O high-minded one: / what various [fates] does a man attain by sinful action?
The Swan said:
Having committed sin, O brahmins, a man goes to hell; / and freed from hell, he enters an animal womb.
Through sins of action born of the body, a man becomes an immovable object; / through those of speech, a bird or a beast; through those of the mind, the lowest caste.
The states of mortals arising from action are declared to be threefold— / high, low, and intermediate—characterised by ten marks.
Coveting the property of others, harbouring malicious thoughts in the mind, / and adherence to false doctrines: this is the threefold action of the mind.
Harshness, untruthfulness, slander in every respect, / and incoherent babble: this is the fourfold [sin] of speech.

वस्त्रापहारकः श्वित्री पङ्गुरश्वापहारकः ॥

अधश्च जायते लोके गां हृत्वा मानवाधमः ॥

गुरुस्वामि द्विजान्क्रोशन्वेदनिन्दां तथैव च ॥

नित्यामयावी भवति तथा चान्नापहारकः ॥
वियोज्यैकमपि प्राणैः प्राणिनं व्याधितस्तथा ॥ 14 ॥
3.51.m:
Taking what is not given, violence outside the ordinance, / and association with another's wife: this is handed down as the threefold [sin] of the body.
Therefore, O brahmins, even when one practices these ten marks in a single [life], / having attained human form through adharma, one becomes miserable.
Here, through evil deeds done in this life, or some through those done previously, / wicked men suffer deformation of form:
A killer of a brahmin becomes consumptive; a violator of the guru's bed has a diseased skin; / a drinker of surā has black teeth; a stealer of gold has deformed nails.
A stealer of clothes suffers from white leprosy; a stealer of horses becomes lame; / so too a stealer of any vehicle should be known as lame.
The lowest of men, having stolen a cow, is born blind in this world; / a stealer of grain has redundant limbs; a thief of speech is mute.
Reviling gurus, masters, and twice-born men, and likewise reviling the Vedas / and listening to it, the evil-minded, lowest of men becomes deaf.
A stealer of food becomes chronically diseased; / and having deprived even a single living being of life, one becomes sick.

ṣaṇḍaśca jāyate loke dārātikramakārakaḥ .. 17 ..
