3.54.d:
तस्य त्यागादवाप्नोति मानवो नरकं धुवम् ॥
समृद्धं स्वामिनं यस्तु सेवित्वा पुरुषाधमः ॥
असमृद्धं त्यजेत्पश्चाद् ध्रुवं नरकमृच्छति ॥ 12 ॥
यो नरः क्लेशमाप्नोति हीनार्थस्वामिसेवनात् ॥
तत्तपोऽस्य विनिर्दष्टं ब्रह्मलोकाय वै द्विजाः ॥ ॥ 13 ॥
कृतज्ञः पुरुषो लोके कृतज्ञः सर्वभाक्तथा ॥
कृतज्ञः सर्वमाप्नोति यत्किञ्चिन्मनसेच्छति ॥ 14 ॥
मातरं पितरं पुत्रं याज्यमृत्विजमेव च ॥
स्वामिनं च गुरुं भृत्यं बान्धवं पशुमेव च ॥ 15 ॥
भार्यां वापि द्विजश्रेष्ठा न त्यजेन्मनसा क्वचित् ॥
एषां तु पतति त्यागे ध्रुवं नरकमृच्छति ॥16॥
न त्यजेत तथैवाग्निं नाग्निमुत्सादयेत्तथा ॥
देवतार्चां तथा विप्रास्त्यक्त्वा नरकमृच्छति॥17॥
छायायां यस्य विश्रान्तो नरः स्यात्पादपस्य तु ॥
तस्मात्पत्रं न हिंसेत कृतज्ञत्वमनुस्मरन् ॥ 18 ॥
3.54.m:
From abandoning it, a human being surely attains hell. / Having served a prosperous master, the vile person / who later abandons him when he is impoverished surely goes to hell.
The man who undergoes distress from serving a master deprived of wealth, / that is prescribed as his austerity for the world of Brahmā, O twice-born.
The grateful man is [a true] person in the world, and the grateful man enjoys all things. / The grateful man attains everything, whatever he desires in his mind.
Mother, father, son, patron of a sacrifice, and sacrificial priest, / master, guru, servant, relative, and animal,
or a wife, O best of twice-born, one should never abandon in thought. / For upon abandoning these, one falls; he surely goes to hell.
Likewise, one should not abandon the sacred fire, nor should one extinguish the sacred fire; / similarly, O brahmins, having abandoned the worship of deities, one goes to hell.
In the shade of whichever tree a person has rested, / he should not harm even a leaf from it, remembering the duty of gratitude.

3.54.s:
kṛtajño bhūtimāpnoti kṛtajñaśca tathā yaśaḥ ..
kṛtajño nākamāpnoti brahmalokamathāpi vā ..19 ..
kṛtajñairvasudhā sarvā dhāryate sumahātmabhiḥ .. 3.270.20 ..
kṛtajña eva yajate kṛtajñastapyate tapaḥ ..
yajvā dātā tathā śūraḥ kṛtajñaśca tathā bhavet ..
kṛtajñastyajate prāṇānmitrakārye tathā dhuvam .. 21 ..
yo brahmalokastapasā na śakyaḥ prāptuṃ dvijendrā mahataḥ sukṛcchrāt ..
taṃ brahma lokaṃ hi naraḥ kṛtajñaḥ prāpnoti śīghraṃ na hi saṃśayo'tra .. 22..
3.54.d:
कृतज्ञो भूतिमाप्नोति कृतज्ञश्च तथा यशः ॥
कृतज्ञो नाकमाप्नोति ब्रह्मलोकमथापि वा ॥19 ॥
कृतज्ञैर्वसुधा सर्वा धार्यते सुमहात्मभिः ॥ 3.270.20 ॥
कृतज्ञ एव यजते कृतज्ञस्तप्यते तपः ॥
यज्वा दाता तथा शूरः कृतज्ञश्च तथा भवेत् ॥
कृतज्ञस्त्यजते प्राणान्मित्रकार्ये तथा धुवम् ॥ 21 ॥
यो ब्रह्मलोकस्तपसा न शक्यः प्राप्तुं द्विजेन्द्रा महतः सुकृच्छ्रात् ॥
तं ब्रह्म लोकं हि नरः कृतज्ञः प्राप्नोति शीघ्रं न हि संशयोऽत्र ॥ 22॥
3.54.m:
The grateful man attains prosperity, and the grateful man likewise attains fame; / the grateful man attains heaven, or the world of Brahmā.
The entire earth is supported by grateful men of exceedingly noble soul.
Only the grateful man sacrifices; the grateful man performs austerity; / a sacrificer, a giver, and a hero should likewise be grateful; / the grateful man also surely gives up his life in the cause of a friend.
The world of Brahmā which cannot be attained even by great, very difficult austerity, O lords of the twice-born, / that world of Brahmā a grateful man attains swiftly; there is no doubt here.

3.55.s:
3.271
haṃsa uvāca..
ācāraḥ svargajanana ācāraḥ kīrtivardhanaḥ ..
ācāraśca tathāyuṣyo dhanyo lokasukhāvahaḥ .. 1 ..
3.55.d:
3.271
हंस उवाच॥
आचारः स्वर्गजनन आचारः कीर्तिवर्धनः ॥
आचारश्च तथायुष्यो धन्यो लोकसुखावहः ॥ 1 ॥
3.55.m: 3.271 / Haṃsa said: / Right conduct produces heaven; right conduct increases fame; / and right conduct grants long life, brings fortune, and yields worldly happiness.

3.55.s:
sarvalakṣaṇahīno'pi sa sadācāravānnaraḥ ..
sarvalakṣaṇalakṣaṇyairvijñeyaḥ puruṣo varaḥ ..2..
3.55.d:
सर्वलक्षणहीनोऽपि स सदाचारवान्नरः ॥
सर्वलक्षणलक्षण्यैर्विज्ञेयः पुरुषो वरः ॥2॥
3.55.m: Even if destitute of all auspicious marks, a man who possesses good conduct / should be understood as superior to men possessing all auspicious marks.

3.55.s:
ācārastrividho loke sevitavyo vicakṣaṇaiḥ ..
śrutismṛtyuditaścaiva sadācārastathā paraḥ ..
ācāraprabhavaṃ saukhyaṃ dhanaṃ ca dvijasattamāḥ ..3..
3.55.d:
आचारस्त्रिविधो लोके सेवितव्यो विचक्षणैः ॥
श्रुतिस्मृत्युदितश्चैव सदाचारस्तथा परः ॥
आचारप्रभवं सौख्यं धनं च द्विजसत्तमाः ॥3॥
3.55.m: Threefold right conduct should be practiced by the discerning in the world: / that taught in the Śruti, [that taught in] the Smṛti, and supreme good conduct. / Happiness and wealth originate from right conduct, O best of twice-born.

3.55.s:
ācārayuktastridivaṃ prayāti ācāravāneva bhavatyarogaḥ ..
ācāravāneva cirantu jīvedācāravāneva bhunakti lakṣmīm .. 4 ..
3.272
haṃsa uvāca ..
śaucaṃ devāḥ praśaṃsanti śaucaṃ brahmarṣayastathā..
śaucayuktena yaddattaṃ tadaśnanti divaukasaḥ ..1..
sarveṣāmeva dharmāṇāṃ śaucaṃ vā phalabhāgbhavet ..
śaucavāneva puruṣo yatheṣṭāṅgatimāpnuyāt .. 2 ..
śarīraśaucaṃ jalamṛdbhiruktamalobhaśaucantu manaḥ pramārṣṭi ..
mano viśuddhaṃ puruṣasya yasya sa lokamāpnoti pitāmahasya .. 3 ..
3.273
.. haṃsa uvāca ..
tīrthānusaraṇaṃ śaucaṃ tīrthānusaraṇaṃ tapaḥ ..
tīrthāmbhobhirnarāḥ pūtā yānti nākamasaṃśayam .. 1 ..
tīrthānusaraṇaṃ puṇyaṃ cādhvanā prāpnuyānnaraḥ ..
adhvanā kṣīṇapāpastu tridivaṃ pratipadyate .. 2 ..
pāpmanāṃ pāpaśamanaṃ vidhatte tapasā vinā ..
vipāpmanā tathā tulyaṃ vidhatte yatprakīrtitam .. 3 ..
3.55.d:
आचारयुक्तस्त्रिदिवं प्रयाति आचारवानेव भवत्यरोगः ॥
आचारवानेव चिरन्तु जीवेदाचारवानेव भुनक्ति लक्ष्मीम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.272
हंस उवाच ॥
शौचं देवाः प्रशंसन्ति शौचं ब्रह्मर्षयस्तथा॥
शौचयुक्तेन यद्दत्तं तदश्नन्ति दिवौकसः ॥1॥
सर्वेषामेव धर्माणां शौचं वा फलभाग्भवेत् ॥
शौचवानेव पुरुषो यथेष्टाङ्गतिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 2 ॥
शरीरशौचं जलमृद्भिरुक्तमलोभशौचन्तु मनः प्रमार्ष्टि ॥
मनो विशुद्धं पुरुषस्य यस्य स लोकमाप्नोति पितामहस्य ॥ 3 ॥
3.273
॥ हंस उवाच ॥
तीर्थानुसरणं शौचं तीर्थानुसरणं तपः ॥
तीर्थाम्भोभिर्नराः पूता यान्ति नाकमसंशयम् ॥ 1 ॥
तीर्थानुसरणं पुण्यं चाध्वना प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥
अध्वना क्षीणपापस्तु त्रिदिवं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 2 ॥
पाप्मनां पापशमनं विधत्ते तपसा विना ॥
विपाप्मना तथा तुल्यं विधत्ते यत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 3 ॥
3.55.m:
Endowed with right conduct, one goes to heaven; possessing right conduct alone, one becomes free of disease; / possessing right conduct alone, one lives long; possessing right conduct alone, one enjoys fortune.
3.272 / Haṃsa said: / The gods praise purity, and so do the brahmin-seers. / What is given by one endowed with purity, the heaven-dwellers eat.
Or rather, purity brings the fruition of all dharmas; / only a man endowed with purity attains the realm he desires.
Bodily purity is taught to be by water and earth, but the purity of freedom from greed cleanses the mind. / The man whose mind is purified attains the world of the Grandfather.
3.273 / Haṃsa said: / Visiting sacred places is purity; visiting sacred places is austerity. / Purified by the waters of sacred places, men go to heaven without a doubt.
Visiting sacred places is holy, and a man should attain it by foot-travel; / with sins exhausted through the travel, he attains heaven.
It accomplishes the quelling of the sin of sinners without austerity; / it makes one equal to a sinless person, as has been proclaimed.

3.55.s:
bahūpakaraṇā yajñā nānāsambhāravistarāḥ ..
na te śakyā daridreṇa prāptuṃ dharmabhṛtāṃvarāḥ .. 4 ..
3.55.d:
बहूपकरणा यज्ञा नानासम्भारविस्तराः ॥
न ते शक्या दरिद्रेण प्राप्तुं धर्मभृतांवराः ॥ 4 ॥
3.55.m: Sacrifices require many implements and elaborate provisions; / they cannot be performed by a poor man, O best among upholders of dharma.

3.55.s:
daridrairanyathā prāptuṃ śakyaṃ yajñaphalaṃ dvijāḥ ..
tīrthānusaraṇaṃ kṛtvā tasmāttīrthaparo bhavet .. 5 ..
3.55.d:
दरिद्रैरन्यथा प्राप्तुं शक्यं यज्ञफलं द्विजाः ॥
तीर्थानुसरणं कृत्वा तस्मात्तीर्थपरो भवेत् ॥ 5 ॥
3.55.m: The fruit of sacrifices can be obtained in another way by the poor, O twice-born, / by visiting sacred places; therefore, one should be devoted to sacred places.

3.55.s:
yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaścaiva susaṃyatam ..
vidyā tapaśca kīrtiśca sa tīrthaphalamaśnute .. 6 ..
3.55.d:
यस्य हस्तौ च पादौ च मनश्चैव सुसंयतम् ॥
विद्या तपश्च कीर्तिश्च स तीर्थफलमश्नुते ॥ 6 ॥
3.55.m: He whose hands, feet, and mind are well controlled, / and who possesses learning, asceticism, and renown, attains the fruit of a sacred ford.

3.55.s:
pāpānāṃ pāpaśamanaṃ dharmavṛddhistathā satām ..
vijñeyaṃ sevitaṃ tīrthaṃ tasmāttīrthaparo bhavet .. 7 ..
3.55.d:
पापानां पापशमनं धर्मवृद्धिस्तथा सताम् ॥
विज्ञेयं सेवितं तीर्थं तस्मात्तीर्थपरो भवेत् ॥ 7 ॥
3.55.m: A sacred ford, when visited, should be known as pacifying the sin of the sinful / and increasing the dharma of the virtuous; therefore, one should be devoted to sacred fords.

3.55.s:
ye sāgnayo dhanopetāstīrthānusaraṇe ratāḥ ..
teṣāṃ yakṣaphalāvāptirvināpi dhanasaṃcayaiḥ .. 8 ..
3.55.d:
ये साग्नयो धनोपेतास्तीर्थानुसरणे रताः ॥
तेषां यक्षफलावाप्तिर्विनापि धनसंचयैः ॥ 8 ॥
3.55.m: Those who maintain the sacrificial fires and possess wealth, yet are devoted to visiting sacred fords, / obtain the fruit of a sacrifice even without accumulations of wealth.

3.55.s:
sarveṣāmeva varṇānāṃ sarvāśramanivāsinām ..
tīrthaṃ phalapradaṃ jñeyaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 9 ..
3.55.d:
सर्वेषामेव वर्णानां सर्वाश्रमनिवासिनाम् ॥
तीर्थं फलप्रदं ज्ञेयं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 9 ॥
3.55.m: A sacred ford should be known to grant its fruit to all castes, / and to those dwelling in all stages of life; there should be no doubt about this.

3.55.s:
kāryāntareṇa yo gatvā snānaṃ tīrthe samācaret ..
tīrthayātrāphalaṃ tasya nāsti snānaphalaṃ tataḥ .. 3.273.10 ..
3.55.d:
कार्यान्तरेण यो गत्वा स्नानं तीर्थे समाचरेत् ॥
तीर्थयात्राफलं तस्य नास्ति स्नानफलं ततः ॥ 3.273.10 ॥
3.55.m: He who goes on other business and happens to bathe in a sacred ford / does not obtain the fruit of a pilgrimage to a sacred ford, [but gets] only the fruit of the bath.

3.55.s:
adhvanāṃ kleśaduḥkhena tīrthayātrāphalaṃ bhavet ..
tīrthānusaraṇaṃ padbhyāṃ tapaḥ paramihocyate .. 11 ..
3.55.d:
अध्वनां क्लेशदुःखेन तीर्थयात्राफलं भवेत् ॥
तीर्थानुसरणं पद्भ्यां तपः परमिहोच्यते ॥ 11 ॥
3.55.m: The fruit of a pilgrimage to a sacred ford comes from the toil and hardship of the roads; / traveling to a sacred ford on foot is called the highest asceticism in this world.

3.55.s:
tadeva kṛtvā yānena snānamātraphalaṃ labhet ..
yasyānye kurvate śaktyā tīrthayātrāṃ tathā naraḥ .. 12 ..
3.55.d:
तदेव कृत्वा यानेन स्नानमात्रफलं लभेत् ॥
यस्यान्ये कुर्वते शक्त्या तीर्थयात्रां तथा नरः ॥ 12 ॥
3.55.m: Doing the same by a vehicle, one obtains merely the fruit of bathing. / If other men undertake a pilgrimage to a sacred ford according to his capacity,

3.55.s:
yānāsanābhyāṃ ca tathā phalaṃ tasya caturguṇam ..
tīrthānusaraṇaṃ kṛtvā kṣetrabhugvijitendriyaḥ ..13..
3.55.d:
यानासनाभ्यां च तथा फलं तस्य चतुर्गुणम् ॥
तीर्थानुसरणं कृत्वा क्षेत्रभुग्विजितेन्द्रियः ॥13॥
3.55.m: and likewise by vehicle and seat, his fruit is fourfold. / Having gone to a sacred ford, one who eats the food of the holy site, with subdued senses,

3.55.s:
phalaṃ prāpnoti viprendrāstīrthāddaśaguṇaṃ bhavet ..
chatropānahahīnastu tathā śataguṇaṃ labhet .. 14 ..
3.55.d:
फलं प्राप्नोति विप्रेन्द्रास्तीर्थाद्दशगुणं भवेत् ॥
छत्रोपानहहीनस्तु तथा शतगुणं लभेत् ॥ 14 ॥
3.55.m: obtains a fruit tenfold greater from the sacred ford, O chiefs of sages; / but one who is without umbrella and shoes obtains a hundredfold.

3.55.s:
chatropānahahīnastu bhaikṣyāśī vijitendriyaḥ ..
mahāpātakajairghoraiḥ kṣipraṃ pāpairvimucyate .. 15 ..
3.55.d:
छत्रोपानहहीनस्तु भैक्ष्याशी विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
महापातकजैर्घोरैः क्षिप्रं पापैर्विमुच्यते ॥ 15 ॥
3.55.m: Moreover, one who is without umbrella and shoes, who eats alms and has subdued his senses, / is quickly freed from terrible sins born of the greatest transgressions.

3.55.s:
na bhaikṣyaṃ parapākaṃ tu na ca bhaikṣyaṃ pratigrahaḥ ..
somapānasamaṃ bhaikṣyaṃ tasmādbhaikṣyaṃ samācaret .. 16 ..
3.55.d:
न भैक्ष्यं परपाकं तु न च भैक्ष्यं प्रतिग्रहः ॥
सोमपानसमं भैक्ष्यं तस्माद्भैक्ष्यं समाचरेत् ॥ 16 ॥
3.55.m: Alms-food is not food cooked by another, nor is alms-food the acceptance of gifts; / alms-food is equal to drinking Soma; therefore one should practice begging alms.

3.55.s:
loke'smindvividhastīrthaḥ svacchando ninditastathā ..
puṣkarādyāstu ye tīrthā svaprabhāvamahattarāḥ .. 17 ..
3.55.d:
लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विविधस्तीर्थः स्वच्छन्दो निन्दितस्तथा ॥
पुष्कराद्यास्तु ये तीर्था स्वप्रभावमहत्तराः ॥ 17 ॥
3.55.m: In this world, a sacred ford is twofold: inherent and designated. / Sacred fords such as Puṣkara are very great by their own inherent power;

3.55.s:
teṣāṃ tīrthaprabhāveṇa kṛtaḥ pūrvaiḥ pratigrahaḥ ..
kaṇvāśramādyā ye tīrthā kaṇvādīnāṃ prabhāvataḥ.. 18 ..
3.55.d:
तेषां तीर्थप्रभावेण कृतः पूर्वैः प्रतिग्रहः ॥
कण्वाश्रमाद्या ये तीर्था कण्वादीनां प्रभावतः॥ 18 ॥
3.55.m: acceptance of gifts was made there by the ancients through the power of those sacred fords. / Sacred fords such as Kaṇva's hermitage [derive their sanctity] from the power of Kaṇva and others.

3.55.s:
puṇyāste kathitā loke pāpaghnāḥ puṇyavṛddhidāḥ ..
dviprakārasya tīrthasya sevā jñeyā mahāphalā .. 19 ..
3.55.d:
पुण्यास्ते कथिता लोके पापघ्नाः पुण्यवृद्धिदाः ॥
द्विप्रकारस्य तीर्थस्य सेवा ज्ञेया महाफला ॥ 19 ॥
3.55.m: They are declared holy in the world, destroying sin and granting an increase of merit. / The veneration of both kinds of sacred ford should be known to yield great fruit.

3.55.s:
ye tīrthasevāniratā dvijeṃdrāste pāpahīnā divamāpnuvanti ..
tatroṣya kālaṃ suciraṃ sukhante mānuṣyaloke sukhamāpnuvanti .. 3.273.20 ..
3.274
haṃsa uvāca ..
bahūpakaraṇā yajñā nānāsambhāravistarāḥ ..
na te śakyā daridreṇa prāptuṃ dharmabhṛtāṃvarāḥ .. 1 ..
daridrairapyathāvāptuṃ śakyaṃ yajñaphalaṃ dvijāḥ ..
sadopavāsanirataistasmādupavasennaraḥ .. 2 ..
yāvanmāsopavāsantu tāvattapa ihocyate ..
anāśakamata ūrdhvaṃ dvijātīnāṃ prakīrtitam .. 3 ..
ṣaṣṭhakālāśanaṃ śūdre tapaḥ paramihocyate ..
varṇasaṃkarajātīnāṃ dinamekaṃ prakīrtitam .. 4 ..
ṣaṣṭhakālātparaṃ śūdrastapaḥ kuryādyathā kvacit ..
rāṣṭre hānistadā jñeyā rājñaścopadravo mahān .. 5 ..
śūdrastu ṣaṣṭhakālāśī yāvacchaktyā tapaścaret ..
māsopavāsādarvāgvā tathā śaktyā dvijaścaret .. 6 ..
3.55.d:
ये तीर्थसेवानिरता द्विजेंद्रास्ते पापहीना दिवमाप्नुवन्ति ॥
तत्रोष्य कालं सुचिरं सुखन्ते मानुष्यलोके सुखमाप्नुवन्ति ॥ 3.273.20 ॥
3.274
हंस उवाच ॥
बहूपकरणा यज्ञा नानासम्भारविस्तराः ॥
न ते शक्या दरिद्रेण प्राप्तुं धर्मभृतांवराः ॥ 1 ॥
दरिद्रैरप्यथावाप्तुं शक्यं यज्ञफलं द्विजाः ॥
सदोपवासनिरतैस्तस्मादुपवसेन्नरः ॥ 2 ॥
यावन्मासोपवासन्तु तावत्तप इहोच्यते ॥
अनाशकमत ऊर्ध्वं द्विजातीनां प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 3 ॥
षष्ठकालाशनं शूद्रे तपः परमिहोच्यते ॥
वर्णसंकरजातीनां दिनमेकं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 4 ॥
षष्ठकालात्परं शूद्रस्तपः कुर्याद्यथा क्वचित् ॥
राष्ट्रे हानिस्तदा ज्ञेया राज्ञश्चोपद्रवो महान् ॥ 5 ॥
शूद्रस्तु षष्ठकालाशी यावच्छक्त्या तपश्चरेत् ॥
मासोपवासादर्वाग्वा तथा शक्त्या द्विजश्चरेत् ॥ 6 ॥
3.55.m:
Those chiefs of the twice-born who are devoted to visiting sacred fords, freed from sin, attain heaven; / and having dwelt there happily for a very long time, they attain happiness in the mortal world.
3.274
Haṃsa said:
Sacrifices require many implements and vast provisions of various materials; / they cannot be performed by a poor man, O foremost of the upholders of dharma.
Yet the fruit of sacrifice can be obtained even by poor men, O twice-born; / a man should fast by being constantly devoted to fasting.
Fasting up to a month is called asceticism here; / beyond that, fasting unto death is proclaimed for the twice-born.
Eating at the sixth mealtime is declared here to be the highest asceticism for a śūdra; / for those of mixed-caste birth, one day is proclaimed.
If a śūdra should ever perform asceticism beyond the sixth mealtime, / it should be known that there is ruin in the kingdom and great affliction for the king.
A śūdra, eating at the sixth mealtime, may practice asceticism according to his ability; / or up to a month's fast, a twice-born may practice according to his ability.

3.55.d:
नास्ति गङ्गासमं तीर्थं नास्ति कृष्णसमा गतिः ॥
गायत्रीसदृशं जप्यं होमं व्याहृतिभिः समम् ॥ 7 ॥
अन्तर्जले तथावाप्तिः पापघ्नमघमर्षणात् ॥
अहिंसासदृशं पुण्यं दानात्संसवनं परम् ॥ 8 ॥
एवमेव द्विजा नास्ति तपो नानशनात्परम् ॥
उपवासैः प्रतप्तानां दीर्घं सुखमनन्तरम् ॥ 9 ॥
उपवासतपःशीला नाकलोकमुपागताः ॥
मोदन्ते त्रिदशे सार्धं यथा देवगणास्तथा ॥ 3.274.10 ॥
पापानां पापशमनं सतामीप्सितकामदम् ॥
उपवासो विनिर्दिष्टो विशेषाद्देवताश्रयः ॥ 11 ॥
उपवासप्रसक्तानां प्रसादसुमुखाः सुराः ॥
यथेच्छमपि जायन्ते नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 12 ॥
वासुदेवमथाश्रित्य नरः सम्यगुपोषितः ॥
अनन्तफलमाप्नोति त्वनन्तः संयतो हरिः ॥ 13 ॥
वासुदेवमथाश्रित्य ब्राह्मणैर्यैरुपोषितम् ॥
तेद्यापि न निवर्तन्ते समुद्रेभ्य इवापगाः ॥ 14 ॥
3.55.m:
There is no sacred ford equal to the Gaṅgā; there is no goal equal to Kṛṣṇa; / there is no recitation equal to the Gāyatrī; [no] oblation equal to [that with] the sacred utterances.
Likewise, [no] achievement in the water destroying sin [is greater] than the Aghamarṣaṇa; / there is no merit equal to non-violence; [no] gift higher than the sacrifice.
Just so, O twice-born, there is no asceticism higher than fasting; / for those heated by fasts, lasting happiness follows immediately.
Disposed to the asceticism of fasting, having reached the heavenly world, / they rejoice together with the gods, just like the hosts of deities.
Fasting is prescribed as pacifying the sin of the sinful and granting the desired wishes of the virtuous, / especially when having a deity as its refuge.
The gods turn gracious faces toward those engaged in fasting, / and even grant their wishes; there should be no doubt about this.
Having taken refuge in Vāsudeva, a man who has properly fasted / obtains endless fruit; for Hari, self-controlled, is endless.
Those brahmins who have fasted after taking refuge in Vāsudeva / do not return even today, like rivers to the oceans.

उपोषिता ये विधिवन्मनुप्यास्ते नाकमासाद्य सुरोषमानाः ॥
देवाङ्गनाभिः सहिता मनुष्या भवन्ति लोके गतसर्वदुःखाः ॥ 15 ॥
3.275
हंस उवाच ॥
मनःसमाधिसंयुक्तस्तीर्थानुसारणात्फलम् ॥
प्राप्नोति सुमहद्विप्रास्तथा सम्यगुपोषितः॥1॥
सर्व एव मनुष्यस्य सर्वकर्मसु साधकम् ॥
मनसा तु विशुद्धेन यद्यदाचरते नरः ॥2॥
न तद्बहुफलं तस्य प्रेत्य चेह च जायते॥
मनो हि परमं भूतं तच्छौचे प्रयतेत्सदा॥3॥
मनःशौचयुतो जन्तुर्नरकं न प्रपद्यते॥
नाकलोकमवाप्नोति त्वथ वा परमं पदम॥4॥
गुणैस्तु सह यो वासो गतदोषस्य मानदाः॥
उपवासस्स विज्ञेयो न शरीरस्य शोषणम्॥5॥
निर्मले सुसुखे शुद्धे सत्यकूले महाह्रदे ॥
स्नातव्यं मानसे तीर्थे तद्धि तीर्थमनुत्तमम् ॥6॥
3.55.m:
Those men who have fasted according to rule, reaching heaven and being honored by the gods, / accompanied by celestial nymphs, become free of all sorrow in that world.
3.275
Haṃsa said:
Endowed with concentration of mind, one obtains very great fruit / from visiting a sacred ford, O brahmins, as also from having properly fasted.
For man, it is [the mind] alone that accomplishes all actions; / whatever a man performs with a purified mind,
[even if little,] yields abundant fruit for him here and in the hereafter. / For the mind is the supreme entity; one should always strive for its purity.
A creature endowed with purity of mind does not fall into hell; / he attains the heavenly world or indeed the supreme abode.
Dwelling with virtues when one's faults have departed, O givers of honor, / should be known as true fasting, not the emaciation of the body.
In the spotless, deeply blissful, pure, great lake whose bank is truth, / one should bathe in the mental sacred ford, for that is the unexcelled sacred ford.

3.55.d:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीमं श्लोकं पौराणमच्युताः ॥
यमो वैवस्वतो देवो यस्तवैष हदि स्थितः ॥
आत्मनश्चाविवादश्चेन्मा गङ्गां मा कुरून्गमः॥7॥
मनो लाघवदं कर्म सततं तु समाचरेत् ॥
सर्वाणि तस्य पुण्यानि भवन्त्यभ्यधिकानि तु ॥8॥
मनःशौचसमायुक्तो यानि मर्त्यो निषेवते॥
मन एव मनुष्यस्य पूर्वरूपाणि शंसति॥9॥
मन एव विजानाति कर्मणो गुरुलाघवम्॥
सत्यं शौचं दमः शौचं शौचं शारीरमेव च॥3.275.10॥
सर्वाणि तस्य शौचानि यस्य शुद्धं मनः सदा ॥
मनःशुद्धिविहीनस्य सर्वे शौचा निरर्थकाः ॥11॥
न तु सा कृत्रिमा शक्या कर्तुं नास्तिक्यवर्जितैः ॥
यस्य दोषपरित्यक्तं गुणाधीनं सदा मनः ॥ 12 ॥
स एव यजते यज्ञैः स एकस्तपते तपः ॥
स एकः सर्वमाप्नोति यत्किञ्चिन्मनसेच्छति॥
तस्माद्धि सर्वशौचानां मनःशौचं परं स्मृतम् ॥13॥

3.55.m:
The self is a river with holy banks, excellent fords, whose water is truth, whose banks are firmness, and whose waves are compassion;
bathed in which the one of meritorious deeds is purified, for the self is truly a sacred ford that is ever enjoyable.

3.276
हंस उवाच ॥

3.56.s:

3.56.m:

Men whose faith is in the gods are declared to be godly, sacrificing to the gods;

3.56.s:

3.56.m:

Of dharma, which has many doors, no rite here is fruitless.
Relying on a pious disposition, endowed with faith, a man

3.56.d:
श्रद्धा पवित्रं परमं हि लोके श्रद्धा शरीरं पुरुषस्य चोक्तम् ॥
श्रद्धां समास्थाय नरश्च कृत्वा पुण्यानि पुण्यां गतिमाप्नुवन्ति ॥ 6 ॥
3.277
हंस उवाच ॥
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं काम्यं क्रियाङ्गं मलकर्षणम् ॥
क्रियास्नानं तथा षष्ठं षोढा स्नानं प्रकीर्त्तितम् ॥1॥
नित्य नैमित्तिकौ कार्यौ उष्णोदकपरोदकैः ॥
तृतीयं च परस्नानं यदुक्तं मलकर्षणम् ॥ 2 ॥
पञ्च पिण्डान्समुद्धृत्य स्नातव्यं परवारिणि ॥
अतो' न्यथा नरः स्नातो दुष्कृतांशेन लिप्यते ॥ 3 ॥
स्नातः शुद्धिमवाप्नोति न तु स्नानफलं नरः ॥
उद्धृत्य पञ्च पिण्डानि स्नातोऽपि परवारिणा ॥ ॥4॥
वह्नितप्ताम्बुना स्नातो नाप्नोति स्नानजं फलम् ॥
स्नातः शुद्धिमवाप्नोति कर्मण्यश्चैव जायते ॥5॥
तस्मात्पुण्येषु तीर्थेषु सागरेषु सरःसु च ॥
सरित्स्वपि च दिव्यासु तथा प्रस्रवणेष्वपि ॥ 6 ॥
3.56.m:
Faith is indeed the supreme purifier in the world, and faith is declared to be the body of man.
Relying on faith and performing meritorious deeds, men attain an auspicious destination.
Haṃsa said:
Obligatory, occasional, optional, forming part of a rite, removing dirt,
and bathing for a rite as the sixth: bathing is proclaimed to be of six kinds.
The obligatory and occasional [baths] may be performed with hot water or with water belonging to another;
and the third bath, which is said to remove dirt, [may be performed in this way as well].
Having lifted out five lumps [of earth], one should bathe in water belonging to another;
otherwise, a man who bathes is tainted with a portion of wrongdoing.
Even when having lifted out five lumps of earth, a man who bathes with water belonging to another
attains purification, but not the fruit of bathing.
One who bathes with water heated by fire does not attain the fruit born of bathing;
having bathed, he attains purification and becomes fit for ritual action.
Therefore, at holy places, in oceans, and in lakes,
in divine rivers, and also in springs,

3.56.s:
dharmārthamācaretsnānaṃ tena nāke mahīyate ..
toyālābhe tathālasye nityanaimittikāvubhau .. 7 ..
3.56.d:
धर्मार्थमाचरेत्स्नानं तेन नाके महीयते ॥
तोयालाभे तथालस्ये नित्यनैमित्तिकावुभौ ॥ 7 ॥
3.56.m:
one should bathe for the sake of dharma; by that, one is exalted in heaven.
If water is unavailable, or likewise in case of lethargy, both the obligatory and occasional,

3.56.s:
malāpakarṣaṇaṃ snānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ca samācaret ..
śuddhimātramavāpnoti taptodakaparodakaiḥ .. 8 ..
3.56.d:
मलापकर्षणं स्नानं तृतीयं च समाचरेत् ॥
शुद्धिमात्रमवाप्नोति तप्तोदकपरोदकैः ॥ 8 ॥
3.56.m:
and thirdly, the bath that removes dirt, may be performed [thus];
one attains mere purification with hot water or with water belonging to another.

3.56.s:
sravanti rātrau chidrāṇi suptasya puruṣasya tu ..
tasmātkalyamathotthāya snānaṃ nityaṃ samācaret ..9..
3.56.d:
स्रवन्ति रात्रौ छिद्राणि सुप्तस्य पुरुषस्य तु ॥
तस्मात्कल्यमथोत्थाय स्नानं नित्यं समाचरेत् ॥9॥
3.56.m:
At night, the bodily apertures of a sleeping person discharge [impurities];
therefore, rising at dawn, one should regularly perform the bath.

3.56.s:
kriyāvaiphalyamāpnoti snānahīnaḥ samācaran ..
yathākathañcitkurvīta snānaṃ nityamato budhaḥ .. 3.277.10 ..
3.56.d:
क्रियावैफल्यमाप्नोति स्नानहीनः समाचरन् ॥
यथाकथञ्चित्कुर्वीत स्नानं नित्यमतो बुधः ॥ 3.277.10 ॥
3.56.m:
One who performs [rites] without having bathed attains fruitlessness of the rites;
therefore, a wise person should somehow perform the bath regularly.

3.56.s:
snātastu tarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā devānāṃ pitṛbhiḥ saha..
snāto bhavati dharmātmā nānyathā snāta ucyate .. 11 ..
3.56.d:
स्नातस्तु तर्पणं कृत्वा देवानां पितृभिः सह॥
स्नातो भवति धर्मात्मा नान्यथा स्नात उच्यते ॥ 11 ॥
3.56.m:
Having bathed and offered libations to the gods together with the ancestors,
the virtuous man is truly bathed; otherwise, he is not said to be bathed.

3.56.s:
sūtake mṛtake snāto na kuryāttarpaṇakriyām ..
mṛtake tarpaṇaṃ kuryānmṛtasyaikasya paṇḍitaḥ .. 12 ..
3.56.d:
सूतके मृतके स्नातो न कुर्यात्तर्पणक्रियाम् ॥
मृतके तर्पणं कुर्यान्मृतस्यैकस्य पण्डितः ॥ 12 ॥
3.56.m:
One who has bathed during impurity from childbirth or from death should not perform the rite of libation;
during impurity from death, a wise person should make the libation for the dead person alone.

3.56.s:
snātaḥ śaucamavāpnoti snānaṃ tuṣṭikaraṃ param ..
bāhyamābhyantaraṃ doṣaṃ snānena praṇudatyapi .. 13 ..
3.56.d:
स्नातः शौचमवाप्नोति स्नानं तुष्टिकरं परम् ॥
बाह्यमाभ्यन्तरं दोषं स्नानेन प्रणुदत्यपि ॥ 13 ॥
3.56.m:
Having bathed, one attains purity; bathing is supremely gratifying;
by bathing, one also drives away external and internal defect.

3.56.s:
duḥsvapnaśamanaṃ snānaṃ cāmaṅgalyapraṇāśanam ..
maṅgalyajananaṃ mukhyaṃ manaḥśaucakaraṃ param .. 14 ..
3.56.d:
दुःस्वप्नशमनं स्नानं चामङ्गल्यप्रणाशनम् ॥
मङ्गल्यजननं मुख्यं मनःशौचकरं परम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.56.m:
Bathing pacifies bad dreams and destroys inauspiciousness;
it generates supreme auspiciousness and supremely brings about mental purity.

3.56.s:
nāpnoti nārakaṃ duḥkhaṃ nityasnāyī narottamaḥ ..
vahnivṛddhikaraṃ snānaṃ snānaṃ saubhāgyavardhanam .. 15 ..
3.56.d:
नाप्नोति नारकं दुःखं नित्यस्नायी नरोत्तमः ॥
वह्निवृद्धिकरं स्नानं स्नानं सौभाग्यवर्धनम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.56.m:
The best of men who bathes daily does not experience the suffering of hell;
bathing promotes the digestive fire; bathing increases good fortune;

3.56.s:
alakṣmyāḥ śamanaṃ snānaṃ snānaṃ duritanāśanam ..
snātaḥ kriyāsamarthaśca tathā bhavati mānavaḥ .. 16 ..
3.56.d:
अलक्ष्म्याः शमनं स्नानं स्नानं दुरितनाशनम् ॥
स्नातः क्रियासमर्थश्च तथा भवति मानवः ॥ 16 ॥
3.56.m:
bathing pacifies misfortune; bathing destroys sin;
and thus bathed, a man becomes capable of ritual actions.

3.56.s:
śirasā tu vinā snāto na snātaḥ parikīrtitaḥ ..
kalye'samarthaḥ snāne tu prāpte bhojanakarmaṇi .. 17 ..
3.56.d:
शिरसा तु विना स्नातो न स्नातः परिकीर्तितः ॥
कल्येऽसमर्थः स्नाने तु प्राप्ते भोजनकर्मणि ॥ 17 ॥
3.56.m:
One who has bathed without his head is not proclaimed to have bathed.
If one is unable to bathe at dawn, then when the mealtime arrives,

3.56.s:
dhruvaṃ samācaretsnānaṃ svargamārgapradarśakama ..
śiraḥsnātastu kurvīta divyaṃ pitryaṃ dvijottama .. 18..
3.56.d:
ध्रुवं समाचरेत्स्नानं स्वर्गमार्गप्रदर्शकम ॥
शिरःस्नातस्तु कुर्वीत दिव्यं पित्र्यं द्विजोत्तम ॥ 18॥
3.56.m:
one should firmly perform bathing, which shows the path to heaven.
Having bathed with the head, O best of the twice-born, one should perform rites for the gods and the ancestors.

3.56.s:
divyapitryāṇi karmāṇi nāsnātastu samācaret ..
vināpi tīrthasalilāddaive paitrye ca karmaṇi ..19 ..
3.56.d:
दिव्यपित्र्याणि कर्माणि नास्नातस्तु समाचरेत् ॥
विनापि तीर्थसलिलाद्दैवे पैत्र्ये च कर्मणि ॥19 ॥
3.56.m:
One should not perform rites for the gods and ancestors without having bathed;
even without holy water, in a rite for gods and ancestors,

3.56.s:
sadā samācaretsnānaṃ dehaśuddhikaraṃ param ..
snānādeva paraṃ puṇyaṃ tīrthasnātaḥ samaśnute .. 3.277.20 ..
3.56.d:
सदा समाचरेत्स्नानं देहशुद्धिकरं परम् ॥
स्नानादेव परं पुण्यं तीर्थस्नातः समश्नुते ॥ 3.277.20 ॥
3.56.m:
one should always perform bathing, which supremely purifies the body;
one who bathes in a holy ford attains supreme merit solely through bathing.

3.56.s:
bhūmiṣṭhantūddhṛtātpuṇyaṃ tasmātprasravaṇodakam ..
tasmācca nairjharantoyaṃ nairjharādapi sārasam .. 21 ..
3.56.d:
भूमिष्ठन्तूद्धृतात्पुण्यं तस्मात्प्रस्रवणोदकम् ॥
तस्माच्च नैर्झरन्तोयं नैर्झरादपि सारसम् ॥ 21 ॥
3.56.m:
Water on the ground is more meritorious than drawn water; spring water is more meritorious than that;
water from a waterfall is more meritorious than that; lake water is even more meritorious than a waterfall;

3.56.s:
sārasādapi nādeyaṃ tasmātsādhuparigraham ..
sarvebhyaśca tathā puṇyaṃ kathitaṃ jāhnavījalam .. 22..
3.56.d:
सारसादपि नादेयं तस्मात्साधुपरिग्रहम् ॥
सर्वेभ्यश्च तथा पुण्यं कथितं जाह्नवीजलम् ॥ 22॥
3.56.m:
river water is more meritorious than lake water; water accepted by virtuous men is more meritorious than that;
and water of the Gaṅgā is declared more meritorious than all.

3.56.s:
gaṅgāplutāṅgā divi devabhogānbhuktvā ciraṃ prāpya manuṣyabhāvam ..
bhavanti loke sukhinaḥ samṛddhā yaśonvitā dharmaparā vidukhāḥ ..23..
3.278
haṃsa uvāca ..
japyaṃ siddhikaraṃ loke dvijānāṃ parikīrtitam ..
japyena siddhimāpnoti viśeṣeṇa dvijottamāḥ..1..
japyenaiva tu saṃsidhyedbrāhmaṇo nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
kuryādanyatra vā kuryānmaitro brāhmaṇa ucyate .. 2 ..
dārvāsane sukhāsīnastvatha vāpi kuśāsane ..
japyaṃ samāhitaḥ kuryādatha vāpi samutthitaḥ .. 3 ..
pūrvottarāśābhimukhaḥ sūryasyābhimukho'pi vā ..
darbhapāṇirdvijaśreṣṭhā jñātvā dharmasya niścayam .. 4 ..
ṛṣiṃ mantrasya vijñāya cchando daivatameva ca ..
viniyogaṃ japaṃ kuryāddhyāyanvai mantradevatām .. 5 ..
nātidrutena kartavyaṃ na caivātivilambitam ..
varṇānuccārayetsarvāñjapyakāle dvijottamāḥ.. 6 ..
3.56.d:
गङ्गाप्लुताङ्गा दिवि देवभोगान्भुक्त्वा चिरं प्राप्य मनुष्यभावम् ॥
भवन्ति लोके सुखिनः समृद्धा यशोन्विता धर्मपरा विदुखाः ॥23॥
3.278
हंस उवाच ॥
जप्यं सिद्धिकरं लोके द्विजानां परिकीर्तितम् ॥
जप्येन सिद्धिमाप्नोति विशेषेण द्विजोत्तमाः॥1॥
जप्येनैव तु संसिध्येद्ब्राह्मणो नात्र संशयः ॥
कुर्यादन्यत्र वा कुर्यान्मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते ॥ 2 ॥
दार्वासने सुखासीनस्त्वथ वापि कुशासने ॥
जप्यं समाहितः कुर्यादथ वापि समुत्थितः ॥ 3 ॥
पूर्वोत्तराशाभिमुखः सूर्यस्याभिमुखोऽपि वा ॥
दर्भपाणिर्द्विजश्रेष्ठा ज्ञात्वा धर्मस्य निश्चयम् ॥ 4 ॥
ऋषिं मन्त्रस्य विज्ञाय च्छन्दो दैवतमेव च ॥
विनियोगं जपं कुर्याद्ध्यायन्वै मन्त्रदेवताम् ॥ 5 ॥
नातिद्रुतेन कर्तव्यं न चैवातिविलम्बितम् ॥
वर्णानुच्चारयेत्सर्वाञ्जप्यकाले द्विजोत्तमाः॥ 6 ॥
3.56.m:
Having bathed their limbs in the Gaṅgā, having enjoyed divine pleasures in heaven for a long time, and then attaining human existence,
they become happy in this world, prosperous, endowed with fame, dedicated to dharma, and free from sorrow.
Haṃsa said:
Recitation is proclaimed in the world to bring accomplishment to the twice-born;
by recitation, O best of the twice-born, one attains accomplishment especially.
A brahmin would certainly attain accomplishment through recitation alone, there is no doubt of this;
whether he performs other [rites] or not, a brahmin is called friendly [to all].
Comfortably seated on a wooden seat or even on a kuśa-grass seat,
one should concentratedly perform recitation, or even standing upright,
facing the east or north, or even facing the sun,
having darbha-grass in hand, O best of the twice-born, having known the certainty of dharma,
having known the seer of the mantra, its metre, its deity,
and its application, one should perform recitation while meditating on the deity of the mantra.
It should not be done too quickly, nor too slowly;
at the time of recitation, O best of the twice-born, one should pronounce all the syllables.

3.56.s:
mantramāvartayedvidvānyathāśakti hyatandritaḥ ..
svādhyāyastu bhavatyuccairupāṃśurjapya ucyate .. 7 ..
manasā tu tathā jāpyaṃ tasmādbahuphalaṃ smṛtam ..
akṣasūtrastu kartavyo rudrākṣairdvijasattamāḥ .. 8 ..
padmākṣairvā mahābhāgāstvatha vā putrajīvakaiḥ ..
muktāphalairvidrumeṇa rukmeṇa sphaṭikena vā ..9..
kuśāguṇena vā viprāḥ samyaggraṃthimatā satā ..
gaṇanaṃ vā tathā kuryātsamyagaṅguliparvabhiḥ ..3.278.10..
evaṃ kṛtvā dvijā japyamavaśyaṃ mantradevatām ..
ārādhya tu tadāpnoti yadyadvāñchati cetasā .. 11 ..
japyena siddhimāsādya brahma lokamavāpnuyāt ..
japyena mucyate pāpājjapyena tridivaṃ vrajet .. 12 ..
japyena mokṣamāpnoti tasmājjapyaparo bhavet ..
akāmakāmaṃ japyena dhruvaṃ mokṣamavāpnuyāt ..13..
3.56.d:
मन्त्रमावर्तयेद्विद्वान्यथाशक्ति ह्यतन्द्रितः ॥
स्वाध्यायस्तु भवत्युच्चैरुपांशुर्जप्य उच्यते ॥ 7 ॥
मनसा तु तथा जाप्यं तस्माद्बहुफलं स्मृतम् ॥
अक्षसूत्रस्तु कर्तव्यो रुद्राक्षैर्द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ 8 ॥
पद्माक्षैर्वा महाभागास्त्वथ वा पुत्रजीवकैः ॥
मुक्ताफलैर्विद्रुमेण रुक्मेण स्फटिकेन वा ॥9॥
कुशागुणेन वा विप्राः सम्यग्ग्रंथिमता सता ॥
गणनं वा तथा कुर्यात्सम्यगङ्गुलिपर्वभिः ॥3.278.10॥
एवं कृत्वा द्विजा जप्यमवश्यं मन्त्रदेवताम् ॥
आराध्य तु तदाप्नोति यद्यद्वाञ्छति चेतसा ॥ 11 ॥
जप्येन सिद्धिमासाद्य ब्रह्म लोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
जप्येन मुच्यते पापाज्जप्येन त्रिदिवं व्रजेत् ॥ 12 ॥
जप्येन मोक्षमाप्नोति तस्माज्जप्यपरो भवेत् ॥
अकामकामं जप्येन ध्रुवं मोक्षमवाप्नुयात् ॥13॥
3.56.m:
The wise man, free from sloth, should repeat the mantra according to his ability.
Vedic study is [performed] aloud, while recitation is said to be in a whisper.
Mental recitation is taught to bear much fruit, even more than that.
A rosary should be made of rudrākṣa beads, O best of the twice-born,
or of lotus seeds, O fortunate ones, or else of putrajīvaka seeds,
of pearls, of coral, of gold, or of crystal,
or, O brahmins, of a cord of kuśa grass properly knotted by a virtuous man;
or one may correctly keep count with the joints of the fingers.
Having performed recitation in this manner, O twice-born, worshipping the deity of the mantra,
one surely attains whatever one desires in one's heart.
Having attained success through recitation, one may reach the world of Brahmā;
through recitation one is freed from evil; through recitation one may go to heaven.
Through recitation one attains liberation; therefore one should be devoted to recitation.
A desireless man surely attains liberation through recitation.

3.56.s:
kāmakāmastadāpnoti yaṃ kāmaṃ manasecchati ..
saṃsiddhā ṛṣayaḥ sarve japyenaiva dvijottamāḥ ..14..
japyaṃ pavitraṃ paramaṃ dvijānāṃ japyena pāpaṃ sakalaṃ jahāti ..
japyena lokām̐llabhate tvabhīṣṭāñjapyena mokṣaṃ labhate dvijātiḥ .. 15 ..
3.279
haṃsa uvāca ..
kṛtvā jalanimagnastu mantrajāpaṃ dvijottamāḥ ..
phalamakṣayamāpnoti mucyate sarvakilbiṣaiḥ .. 1 ..
mantramantarjale japyaṃ dhyāyatā mantradevatām ..
naraṃ mocayate pāpānmahāpātakajādapi .. 2 ..
antarjalenātha vidhūtapāpā dvijāstu nākaṃ dhruvameva yānti ..
jale nimagnena tatastu yatnānmantrasya jāpaḥ puruṣeṇa kāryaḥ .. 3 ..
3.280
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
recakaṃ pūrakaṃ caiva kumbhakaṃ ca tathā dvijāḥ ..
ekastryavastho vijñeyaḥ prāṇāyāmo mahāphalaḥ .. 1 ..
3.56.d:
कामकामस्तदाप्नोति यं कामं मनसेच्छति ॥
संसिद्धा ऋषयः सर्वे जप्येनैव द्विजोत्तमाः ॥14॥
जप्यं पवित्रं परमं द्विजानां जप्येन पापं सकलं जहाति ॥
जप्येन लोकाम्̐ल्लभते त्वभीष्टाञ्जप्येन मोक्षं लभते द्विजातिः ॥ 15 ॥
3.279
हंस उवाच ॥
कृत्वा जलनिमग्नस्तु मन्त्रजापं द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
फलमक्षयमाप्नोति मुच्यते सर्वकिल्बिषैः ॥ 1 ॥
मन्त्रमन्तर्जले जप्यं ध्यायता मन्त्रदेवताम् ॥
नरं मोचयते पापान्महापातकजादपि ॥ 2 ॥
अन्तर्जलेनाथ विधूतपापा द्विजास्तु नाकं ध्रुवमेव यान्ति ॥
जले निमग्नेन ततस्तु यत्नान्मन्त्रस्य जापः पुरुषेण कार्यः ॥ 3 ॥
3.280
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
रेचकं पूरकं चैव कुम्भकं च तथा द्विजाः ॥
एकस्त्र्यवस्थो विज्ञेयः प्राणायामो महाफलः ॥ 1 ॥
3.56.m:
One who desires desires attains whatever desire he wishes for in his mind.
All the sages achieved perfection solely through recitation, O best of the twice-born.
Recitation is the supreme purifier of the twice-born; through recitation one abandons all evil;
through recitation one obtains desired worlds; through recitation a twice-born man attains liberation.
3.279
Haṃsa said:
Having performed the recitation of a mantra submerged in water, O best of the twice-born,
one obtains imperishable fruit and is freed from all sins.
A mantra repeated underwater by one meditating on the deity of the mantra
liberates a man from evil, even from that born of heinous sins.
Twice-born whose sins are washed away by the water within surely go to heaven.
Therefore, submerged in water, a man should diligently perform the recitation of the mantra.
3.280
Haṃsa said:
Exhalation, inhalation, and also retention, O twice-born:
breath control is to be understood as single, possessing three states, and bearing great fruit.

3.56.s:
ādadānastu yaḥ śvāsaṃ maṃtrādhyayanamācaret ..
manasā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhā recakaṃ tatprakīrtitam .. 2 ..
śvāsa sandhāraṇaṃ kurvannādadāno na ca tyajan ..
pūrakaṃ tadvinirdiṣṭaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam .. 3 ..
maṃtrasya devatādhyānaṃ prāṇāyāmaṃ tathā caret ..
prāṇāyāmātparaṃ nāsti dvijātīnāṃ tathā tapaḥ .. 4 ..
nirodhājjāyate vāyustatastvagniḥ prajāyate ..
tatastu salilaṃ dehe pūyate taistribhirnaraḥ .. 5 ..
ākeśāgraṃ nakhāgraṃ svaṃ tapsyate paramaṃ tapaḥ ..
yastu kuryād dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ prāṇāyāmamatandritaḥ .. 6 ..
na tatpuṇyamavāpnoti tīrthānusaraṇāddvijāḥ ..
na yajñena tathā kṛcchraiḥ prāṇāyāmādyadāpnuyāt ..7 ..
prāṇāyāmaparā viprāḥ sarvanirdhautakalmaṣāḥ ..
tridivaṃ pratipadyante mokṣaṃ vā manasepsitam ..8..
3.56.d:
आददानस्तु यः श्वासं मंत्राध्ययनमाचरेत् ॥
मनसा ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठा रेचकं तत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 2 ॥
श्वास सन्धारणं कुर्वन्नाददानो न च त्यजन् ॥
पूरकं तद्विनिर्दिष्टं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥ 3 ॥
मंत्रस्य देवताध्यानं प्राणायामं तथा चरेत् ॥
प्राणायामात्परं नास्ति द्विजातीनां तथा तपः ॥ 4 ॥
निरोधाज्जायते वायुस्ततस्त्वग्निः प्रजायते ॥
ततस्तु सलिलं देहे पूयते तैस्त्रिभिर्नरः ॥ 5 ॥
आकेशाग्रं नखाग्रं स्वं तप्स्यते परमं तपः ॥
यस्तु कुर्याद् द्विजश्रेष्ठाः प्राणायाममतन्द्रितः ॥ 6 ॥
न तत्पुण्यमवाप्नोति तीर्थानुसरणाद्द्विजाः ॥
न यज्ञेन तथा कृच्छ्रैः प्राणायामाद्यदाप्नुयात् ॥7 ॥
प्राणायामपरा विप्राः सर्वनिर्धौतकल्मषाः ॥
त्रिदिवं प्रतिपद्यन्ते मोक्षं वा मनसेप्सितम् ॥8॥
3.56.m:
Taking in the breath, when one performs the study of the mantra
with the mind, O best of brahmins, that is proclaimed as recaka.
Holding the breath, neither taking it in nor releasing it,
that is declared as pūraka, destroying all blemishes.
One should thus practice breath control while meditating on the deity of the mantra;
there is no austerity for the twice-born higher than breath control.
From retention wind is generated, and from that fire is born;
then water [is generated] in the body; by these three, a man is purified.
One who, free from sloth, performs breath control, O best of the twice-born,
will practice the highest austerity from the tip of his hair to the tip of his nails.
The merit one attains from breath control is not obtained
from visiting holy bathing places, O twice-born, nor through sacrifice, nor through penances.
Brahmins devoted to breath control, all their blemishes washed away,
attain heaven or the liberation desired by their mind.

3.56.s:
prāṇāyāmena naśyanti mahāpātakajānyapi ..
ghorāpyenāṃsi dharmajñāḥ prāṇāyāmamataścaret .. 9 ..
etattapastatparamaṃ dvijānāṃ pāpāpahaṃ puṇyavivṛddhikāri ..
mokṣapradaṃ vā puruṣottamānāṃ tasmātprayatnena samācarettat .. 3.280.10 ..
3.56.d:
प्राणायामेन नश्यन्ति महापातकजान्यपि ॥
घोराप्येनांसि धर्मज्ञाः प्राणायाममतश्चरेत् ॥ 9 ॥
एतत्तपस्तत्परमं द्विजानां पापापहं पुण्यविवृद्धिकारि ॥
मोक्षप्रदं वा पुरुषोत्तमानां तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन समाचरेत्तत् ॥ 3.280.10 ॥
3.56.m:
Through breath control even terrible evils born of heinous sins are destroyed,
O knowers of dharma; therefore one should practice breath control.
This is the supreme austerity for the twice-born, dispelling evil and increasing merit,
bestowing liberation upon the best of men; therefore one should practice it with effort.

3.57.s:
3.281
haṃsa uvāca ..
viṣayebhyaḥ pravṛttasya cetaso vinivartanam ..
pratyāhāraṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ paramantattapaḥ smṛtam ..1..
3.57.d:
3.281
हंस उवाच ॥
विषयेभ्यः प्रवृत्तस्य चेतसो विनिवर्तनम् ॥
प्रत्याहारं विनिर्दिष्टं परमन्तत्तपः स्मृतम् ॥1॥
3.57.m:
3.281
Haṃsa said:
The withdrawal of the mind that has gone out toward sensory objects
is designated as withdrawal [of the senses]; that is traditionally held to be the supreme austerity.

3.57.s:
atyantacañcalaṃ cittaṃ tasya saṃyamanaṃ dvijāḥ ..
pratyāhāreṇa kartavyaṃ puruṣeṇa vipaścitā ..2..
3.57.d:
अत्यन्तचञ्चलं चित्तं तस्य संयमनं द्विजाः ॥
प्रत्याहारेण कर्तव्यं पुरुषेण विपश्चिता ॥2॥
3.57.m:
The mind is exceedingly fickle; the restraint of it, O twice-born,
should be performed through withdrawal [of the senses] by a wise man.

3.57.s:
pratyāhṛtya naraścetaḥ kāmebhyo dvijasattamāḥ ..
kāmānāṃ bhājanaṃ loke mokṣasya ca tathā bhavet ..3..
3.57.d:
प्रत्याहृत्य नरश्चेतः कामेभ्यो द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
कामानां भाजनं लोके मोक्षस्य च तथा भवेत् ॥3॥
3.57.m:
Having withdrawn the mind from desires, O best of the twice-born,
a man becomes a vessel for [true] desires in this world and for liberation.

3.57.s:
vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumām̐ścarati nispṛhaḥ..
nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati ..4..
3.57.d:
विहाय कामान्यः सर्वान्पुमाम्̐श्चरति निस्पृहः॥
निर्ममो निरहंकारः स शान्तिमधिगच्छति ॥4॥
3.57.m:
Having abandoned all desires, the man who walks about free from longing,
without mine-ness and without egoism, attains peace.

3.57.s:
pratyāhāraṃ yathā kuryātkāmebhyaścetaso naraḥ ..
yathākāmamavāpnoti mokṣopāyaṃ ca vindati..5..
3.57.d:
प्रत्याहारं यथा कुर्यात्कामेभ्यश्चेतसो नरः ॥
यथाकाममवाप्नोति मोक्षोपायं च विन्दति॥5॥
3.57.m:
When a man performs withdrawal of the mind from desires,
he obtains [everything] according to his wish and finds the means to liberation.

3.57.s:
cañcalaṃ hi mano viprāḥ pramāthi balavaddṛḍham ..
tasya yatnaṃ samāsthāya kartavyo nigraho budhaiḥ..6..
3.57.d:
चञ्चलं हि मनो विप्राः प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् ॥
तस्य यत्नं समास्थाय कर्तव्यो निग्रहो बुधैः॥6॥
3.57.m:
For the mind is fickle, turbulent, powerful, and obstinate, O brahmins;
the wise must apply effort to its restraint.

3.57.s:
yāvanna ceta āyāti vairāgyaṃ paramaṃ naraḥ..
tāvanna śakto bhavati pratyāhārasya vai dvijāḥ ..7..
3.57.d:
यावन्न चेत आयाति वैराग्यं परमं नरः॥
तावन्न शक्तो भवति प्रत्याहारस्य वै द्विजाः ॥7॥
3.57.m:
As long as a man's mind does not reach supreme dispassion,
so long is he unable to achieve withdrawal [of the senses], O twice-born.

3.57.s:
janmamṛtyujarāvyādhiduḥkhaśokārditaṃ jagat ..
paśyankhinnastadā viprā vairāgyātsiddhimāpnuyāt .. 8 ..
3.57.d:
जन्ममृत्युजराव्याधिदुःखशोकार्दितं जगत् ॥
पश्यन्खिन्नस्तदा विप्रा वैराग्यात्सिद्धिमाप्नुयात् ॥ 8 ॥
3.57.m:
Seeing the world afflicted by birth, death, old age, disease, pain, and grief,
depressed by this, O brahmins, one attains perfection through dispassion.

3.57.s:
anityatāṃ tathā paśyañjagato'sya punaḥpunaḥ..
vairāgyabhāvamāsthāya tataḥ siddhimavāpnuyāt..9..
3.57.d:
अनित्यतां तथा पश्यञ्जगतोऽस्य पुनःपुनः॥
वैराग्यभावमास्थाय ततः सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात्॥9॥
3.57.m:
Seeing again and again the impermanence of this world,
and resorting to the state of dispassion, one then attains perfection.

3.57.s:
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca rājñāṃ bhūtagaṇasya ca..
dṛṣṭvā kṣayaṃ mahābhāgā virakto vipramucyate..3.281.10..
3.57.d:
देवतानामृषीणां च राज्ञां भूतगणस्य च॥
दृष्ट्वा क्षयं महाभागा विरक्तो विप्रमुच्यते॥3.281.10॥
3.57.m:
Having witnessed the destruction of deities, sages, kings, and the host of living beings,
O fortunate ones, one becomes detached and is freed.

3.57.s:
garbhavāse mahadduḥkhaṃ narake ca punaḥpunaḥ..
tiryagyonau ca mānuṣye tiryakkāmo vimucyate ..11..
3.57.d:
गर्भवासे महद्दुःखं नरके च पुनःपुनः॥
तिर्यग्योनौ च मानुष्ये तिर्यक्कामो विमुच्यते ॥11॥
3.57.m:
There is great suffering in living in the womb, and repeatedly in hell,
and in animal wombs, and in human birth; one whose desires are crooked is released [from them].

3.57.s:
divasedivase khinno parānneṣu ca yo dvijāḥ ..
vairāgyamāpnoti tathā khinno mūtrapurīṣayoḥ..12..
3.57.d:
दिवसेदिवसे खिन्नो परान्नेषु च यो द्विजाः ॥
वैराग्यमाप्नोति तथा खिन्नो मूत्रपुरीषयोः॥12॥
3.57.m:
He who is afflicted day after day by [eating] the food of others, O twice-born,
and who is disgusted with urine and feces, attains dispassion.

3.57.s:
duḥkhānāṃ tu pratīghāte sukhamityeva bhāvite ..
duḥkhebhyaḥ svalpakālena yaḥ khinnaḥ sa virajyate .. 13 ..
3.57.d:
दुःखानां तु प्रतीघाते सुखमित्येव भाविते ॥
दुःखेभ्यः स्वल्पकालेन यः खिन्नः स विरज्यते ॥ 13 ॥
3.57.m:
When the warding off of sufferings is merely imagined to be happiness,
he who is wearied of sufferings in a short time becomes detached.

3.57.s:
virāgamāsthāya tataḥ pratyāhāramatandritaḥ ..
kāmebhyaścetasaḥ kuryāttena sarvaṃ samaśnute ..14..
3.57.d:
विरागमास्थाय ततः प्रत्याहारमतन्द्रितः ॥
कामेभ्यश्चेतसः कुर्यात्तेन सर्वं समश्नुते ॥14॥
3.57.m:
Then, having resorted to dispassion, he should diligently withdraw
the mind from desires; through that he obtains everything.

3.57.s:
āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat ..
tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī .. 15 ..
3.282
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
ekatra samavasthānaṃ bāhye dravye tu cetasaḥ ..
dhāraṇā sā vinirdiṣṭā manaso bandhakārikā .. 1 ..
sā kāryā devatārcāyāṃ yatrāsya syātsthirā matiḥ ..
ekatra labdhvā lakṣyaṃ tu manasaścañcalasya tu .. 2 ..
turyannivāraṇaṃ yatnānmano'nugrahakāraṇāt ..
atha vā lakṣyabandhantu bhuvi kāryaṃ vijānatā .. 3 ..
labdhalakṣastu bhūyoge mahīyogaṃ samutsṛjet ..
labdhalakṣyo naraḥ kuryānnarāstejasi sattamāḥ .. 4 ..
samutsṛjya tato vāyau tato nabhasi kārayet ..
kramaśastvevamāruhya lakṣyaṃ lakṣyatayā naraḥ .. 5 ..
bāhyeṣu dhāraṇāṃ kṛtvā manasaḥ siddhimaśnute ..
manasaścañcalasyāsya yāvadbandhanadhāraṇā ..6 ..
3.57.d:
आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् ॥
तद्वत्कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ॥ 15 ॥
3.282
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
एकत्र समवस्थानं बाह्ये द्रव्ये तु चेतसः ॥
धारणा सा विनिर्दिष्टा मनसो बन्धकारिका ॥ 1 ॥
सा कार्या देवतार्चायां यत्रास्य स्यात्स्थिरा मतिः ॥
एकत्र लब्ध्वा लक्ष्यं तु मनसश्चञ्चलस्य तु ॥ 2 ॥
तुर्यन्निवारणं यत्नान्मनोऽनुग्रहकारणात् ॥
अथ वा लक्ष्यबन्धन्तु भुवि कार्यं विजानता ॥ 3 ॥
लब्धलक्षस्तु भूयोगे महीयोगं समुत्सृजेत् ॥
लब्धलक्ष्यो नरः कुर्यान्नरास्तेजसि सत्तमाः ॥ 4 ॥
समुत्सृज्य ततो वायौ ततो नभसि कारयेत् ॥
क्रमशस्त्वेवमारुह्य लक्ष्यं लक्ष्यतया नरः ॥ 5 ॥
बाह्येषु धारणां कृत्वा मनसः सिद्धिमश्नुते ॥
मनसश्चञ्चलस्यास्य यावद्बन्धनधारणा ॥6 ॥
3.57.m:
Just as waters enter the ocean, which is filled from all sides and firmly fixed,
even so all desires enter him; he attains peace, not the craver of desires.
3.282
The Haṃsa said:
The steady fixation of the mind upon a single external object
is taught as concentration, which causes the binding of the mind.
It should be practiced upon an image of a deity where one's intellect may become steady.
Having obtained a single target for the fickle mind,
one should strive diligently for its restraint for the sake of subduing the mind.
Or, the wise man should make the binding of the target upon the earth.
Having obtained the target in the practice upon earth, he should abandon the practice upon earth.
Having obtained the target, O best of men, a man should practice upon fire.
Having abandoned [that], he should then cause [the mind to focus] on wind, and then on space.
Ascending in this manner step by step, a man, taking target after target,
having practiced concentration on external objects, attains mastery of the mind.
As long as the binding concentration of this fickle mind [is unachieved],

3.57.s:
tāvaddhyānamathārūḍhaṃ na śakyaṃ kenaciddvijāḥ ..
dhāraṇāṃ niścalāṃ prāpya tato dhyānamavāpnuyāt .. 7 ..
śarīraṃ vijahātyenaṃ yatra baddhā tu dhāraṇā ..
prāpnoti tanmayībhāvaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 8 ..
saṃprāpya dhāraṇāṃ muktvā śarīraṃ manujottamaḥ ..
kālānmokṣamavāpnoti dhyānācchīghramiti sthitiḥ .. 9 ..
prāptastu yanmayībhāvaṃ dhāraṇāsthaḥ pumāṃstataḥ ..
sa yadā puruṣaṃ yāti tadā sa pratipadyate .. 3.282.10 ..
dhruve mokṣamavāpnoti dhāraṇāṃ prāpya mānavaḥ ..
kintu kālena mahatā dhyānācchīghramiti sthitiḥ .. 11 ..
sarvaloke tathā jñeyā bāhyadravyavināśanāḥ ..
teṣāntu dhāraṇā kāryā manograhaṇakāraṇam .. 12 ..
saṃprāpya manaso bandhaṃ niścalaṃ puruṣottamaḥ ..
dhāraṇāyogatastasmāddhruvaṃ mokṣamupāśnute .. 13 ..
3.57.d:
तावद्ध्यानमथारूढं न शक्यं केनचिद्द्विजाः ॥
धारणां निश्चलां प्राप्य ततो ध्यानमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 7 ॥
शरीरं विजहात्येनं यत्र बद्धा तु धारणा ॥
प्राप्नोति तन्मयीभावं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 8 ॥
संप्राप्य धारणां मुक्त्वा शरीरं मनुजोत्तमः ॥
कालान्मोक्षमवाप्नोति ध्यानाच्छीघ्रमिति स्थितिः ॥ 9 ॥
प्राप्तस्तु यन्मयीभावं धारणास्थः पुमांस्ततः ॥
स यदा पुरुषं याति तदा स प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 3.282.10 ॥
ध्रुवे मोक्षमवाप्नोति धारणां प्राप्य मानवः ॥
किन्तु कालेन महता ध्यानाच्छीघ्रमिति स्थितिः ॥ 11 ॥
सर्वलोके तथा ज्ञेया बाह्यद्रव्यविनाशनाः ॥
तेषान्तु धारणा कार्या मनोग्रहणकारणम् ॥ 12 ॥
संप्राप्य मनसो बन्धं निश्चलं पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
धारणायोगतस्तस्माद्ध्रुवं मोक्षमुपाश्नुते ॥ 13 ॥
3.57.m:
so long meditation, when mounted, cannot be accomplished by anyone, O twice-born.
Having attained motionless concentration, one may then attain meditation.
Where concentration has been fixed, when one leaves this body,
one attains identity with that; there should be no doubt here.
Having attained concentration, a best of men, having cast off his body,
attains liberation in time; but through meditation [it comes] quickly: such is the rule.
A man established in concentration, having attained identity with that,
when he goes to the Cosmic Person, then he realizes [Him].
Having attained concentration, a man attains liberation certainly,
but after a long time; through meditation [it comes] quickly: such is the rule.
Likewise, in all the world, external objects are to be known as perishable;
concentration should be practiced upon them for the sake of seizing the mind.
Having attained the motionless binding of the mind, the best of men,
from that practice of concentration, surely attains liberation.

3.57.s:
yadasya nityaṃ hadi saṃsthitaṃ syāttatsyāttadevāsya hi mṛtyukāle ..
yadbhāvayatyeva hi mṛtyukāle bhavatyavaśyaṃ sa hi tanmayastu .. 14 ..
3.283
haṃsa uvāca ..
dravye tu dhāraṇā bāhye dhāraṇā parikīrtitā ..
saiva cetasi nirdiṣṭā dhyāneti manujottamāḥ.. 1 ..
adhomukhaṃ hṛtkamale karṇikāyāṃ dvijottamāḥ..
dhyānaṃ sūryasya kurvīta tejorāśervicakṣaṇaḥ..2..

3.57.m:
What is constantly established in one's heart, that indeed will be there at the time of death;
and whatever one contemplates at the time of death, with that he indeed inevitably becomes one.
3.283
The Haṃsa said:
Concentration upon an external object is proclaimed as concentration;
that very same [focus] within the mind, O best of men, is designated as meditation.
On the pericarp of the downward-facing heart-lotus, O best of the twice-born,
a wise man should perform meditation on the sun, the mass of splendour.
Within the sun is situated the moon, within the moon the fire;
within the splendour is situated the essence, more intensely luminous even than splendour.
In its midst is Lord Viṣṇu, the eternal Supreme Self,
the infallible Cosmic Person, ever all-pervading, the Great Lord.
One should behold Him, subtler than the subtlest, whose form is splendour, difficult to approach;
having seen Him through the discipline of meditation, a man attains perfection.
Assuming unwearied one of the yogic postures:
the svastika, sarvatobhadra, paryaṅka, or lotus posture,

3.57.m:
One should know that Supreme Cosmic Person as devoid of sound, touch, and taste,
and free from smell and form, having gone to whom one does not grieve.
Devoid [of mental activity], intent on meditation, O brahmins, it is proclaimed as samādhi;
having attained it, he is never overcome by other men.
There is no happiness higher than samādhi anywhere in the three worlds;
and established in samādhi, one is not moved even by heavy sorrow.
Even if conches by the hundreds are blown in his ears,
and if kettle-drums are beaten, he does not perceive external sound.
Likewise, struck with blows, or with his body burned by fire,
or standing in intense, dreadful cold, he does not perceive external touch.
What need is there to speak of victory over external smell or taste for such a one?
He who, having seen the Self by the self, again attains samādhi,
neither thirst nor hunger ever assails him;
even as he abandons thirst, not eating, he observes [the Self].

3.57.m:
That best of men knows only one distress:
rising from samādhi—by that he is deeply tormented.
That happiness which a man obtains upon attaining motionless samādhi / is not in heaven, nor in the netherworld, nor among human beings.
Upon attaining samādhi and abandoning the bondage of the body, a person / pervades all the worlds, the three worlds with the moving and unmoving.
And that person pervades whatever is even outside the three worlds; / upon attaining samādhi, a human being attains infinity.
Free from birth, death, old age, disease, grief, and suffering, / all-pervading, destroying everything, consisting of the qualities of all senses,
everywhere and at all times, O brahmins, he is in that [state]—there is no doubt about this; / he then attains the nature of the Cosmic Person and attains all power.
Restraining the mind indeed in fixations, ascending then afterwards to meditation, / and abiding in samādhi, the high-minded one attains equality with the Supreme Person.

3.285 / The sages said: / That which is the root of the attainment of the great state, O best of the twice-born, / declare all of that to us, marked by direct perception.
Haṃsa said: / All men who are guided by resolve attain it; / there is nothing in the world exceedingly difficult to obtain for those who have resolve as their second.
Resolve is the highest kinsman; a companion comes next; / endowed with that, a man attains [it] completely; this is certain.
In dharma, in wealth, in pleasure, and in liberation, O best of sages, / a man who possesses resolve is always to be known as a vessel.
For those destitute of resolve, even a slight objective is hard to attain; / for those who lack resolve, being lazy and wicked-minded,
wealth, even when seized in hand, is destroyed suddenly and quickly; / one who is destitute of resolve is no better than a tree-trunk.
Therefore, men who are devoted to diligent effort are declared in the world to be enjoyers of their desires; / theirs is both this world and the other, and likewise the path to liberation is not far for them.
