yunakti vyavasāyena paścājjñeyaḥ sa paṃḍitaḥ .. 4 ..
3.58.d:
आदौ निश्चित्य यत्कर्म मनसा बुद्धिमान्नरः ॥
युनक्ति व्यवसायेन पश्चाज्ज्ञेयः स पंडितः ॥ 4 ॥
3.58.m: An intelligent man who first determines an action with his mind / and then engages [in it] with resolve is to be known as wise.

3.58.s:
yāvanto niścitāstvarthā manasā kenacitkvacit ..
tāvanna śakyate kartuṃ saṃkalpo'taḥ paro mataḥ .. 5 ..
3.58.d:
यावन्तो निश्चितास्त्वर्था मनसा केनचित्क्वचित् ॥
तावन्न शक्यते कर्तुं संकल्पोऽतः परो मतः ॥ 5 ॥
3.58.m: As many ends as have been decided in the mind by anyone anywhere, / so many can be accomplished; therefore intention is regarded as supreme.

3.58.s:
saṃkalpitānāṃ manasā tu pūrvaṃ siddhiḥ pradiṣṭā vyavasāyayuktā ..
kāryāṇi sarvāṇi tatastu loke saṃkalpamūlāni vadaṃti santaḥ .. 6 ..
3.287
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ ..
naiḥśreyasapadāvāptau pratyāhārastvayeritaḥ ..
dhāraṇādhyānayogaśca samādhirapi cottamā .. 1 ..
bhūya eva tvamācakṣva nṛṇāṃ saṃsārasāriṇām ..
hitārthamuttamaṃ mārgaṃ lokadvayasukhāvaham .. 2 ..
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
agnirmukhaṃ devatānāṃ sarvabhūtaparāyaṇam ..
tasya śuśrūṣaṇādeva sarvānkāmānsamaśnute .. 3 ..
sā mūrtiḥ paramā viṣṇostaddattaṃ prāpnute raviḥ ..
sūryādvṛṣṭistatastvannamannātprabhavate jagat .. 4 ..
adhaḥpravarṣiṇo devā bhaumāstūrdhvaṃ pravarṣiṇaḥ ..
ūrdhvapravarṣiṇaṃ mukhyaṃ bhaumaṃ dattaṃ hutāśane .. 5 ..
oṃkāraṃ pūrvamuddiśya yāṃyāṃ viprastu devatām ..
havirjuhoti sā tasya prītā bhavati nityadā .. 6 ..
3.58.d:
संकल्पितानां मनसा तु पूर्वं सिद्धिः प्रदिष्टा व्यवसाययुक्ता ॥
कार्याणि सर्वाणि ततस्तु लोके संकल्पमूलानि वदंति सन्तः ॥ 6 ॥
3.287
ऋषय ऊचुः ॥
नैःश्रेयसपदावाप्तौ प्रत्याहारस्त्वयेरितः ॥
धारणाध्यानयोगश्च समाधिरपि चोत्तमा ॥ 1 ॥
भूय एव त्वमाचक्ष्व नृणां संसारसारिणाम् ॥
हितार्थमुत्तमं मार्गं लोकद्वयसुखावहम् ॥ 2 ॥
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
अग्निर्मुखं देवतानां सर्वभूतपरायणम् ॥
तस्य शुश्रूषणादेव सर्वान्कामान्समश्नुते ॥ 3 ॥
सा मूर्तिः परमा विष्णोस्तद्दत्तं प्राप्नुते रविः ॥
सूर्याद्वृष्टिस्ततस्त्वन्नमन्नात्प्रभवते जगत् ॥ 4 ॥
अधःप्रवर्षिणो देवा भौमास्तूर्ध्वं प्रवर्षिणः ॥
ऊर्ध्वप्रवर्षिणं मुख्यं भौमं दत्तं हुताशने ॥ 5 ॥
ओंकारं पूर्वमुद्दिश्य यांयां विप्रस्तु देवताम् ॥
हविर्जुहोति सा तस्य प्रीता भवति नित्यदा ॥ 6 ॥
3.58.m:
For things first intended by the mind, success accompanied by resolve has been taught; / therefore, the virtuous say that all undertakings in the world have their root in intention.
3.287 / The sages said: / For the attainment of the state of the highest good, withdrawal of the senses has been spoken by you, / as well as the yoga of fixation and meditation, and also excellent samādhi.
Declare again to us, for the benefit of men moving in the cycle of existence, / the supreme path that brings happiness in both worlds.
Haṃsa said: / Fire is the mouth of the deities, the refuge of all beings; / only through serving it does one enjoy all desires.
It is the supreme form of Viṣṇu; what is given to it, the sun receives; / from the sun comes rain, then from that comes food, and from food the world arises.
The gods rain downward, but earthly beings rain upward; / what is given by earthly beings into the fire is principal, raining upward.
Whatever deity a brahmin offers an oblation to, / having first uttered the syllable Oṃ, that [deity] becomes always pleased with him.

3.58.s:
vahnidattena haviṣā tṛptimāyānti devatāḥ ..
tāstṛptāstarpayantyenaṃ naraṃ kāmasamṛddhibhiḥ .. 7 ..
3.58.d:
वह्निदत्तेन हविषा तृप्तिमायान्ति देवताः ॥
तास्तृप्तास्तर्पयन्त्येनं नरं कामसमृद्धिभिः ॥ 7 ॥
3.58.m: The deities attain satisfaction through the oblation given into the fire; / satisfied, they satisfy that man with abundances of desires.

3.58.s:
sūrye homaḥ paraḥ puṇyastena svarge mahīyate ..
tasmādaṣṭaguṇaṃ puṇyamidhmabhiḥ prāpnuyāddhute .. 8 ..
3.58.d:
सूर्ये होमः परः पुण्यस्तेन स्वर्गे महीयते ॥
तस्मादष्टगुणं पुण्यमिध्मभिः प्राप्नुयाद्धुते ॥ 8 ॥
3.58.m: An oblation offered to the sun is supremely meritorious; through it one is exalted in heaven; / eight times that merit one would obtain when offering with firewood.

3.58.s:
tasmāddaśaguṇaṃ sasyairvrīhibhirdviguṇaṃ tataḥ ..
tāvadeva tathā puṇyaṃ home siddhārthakaiḥ smṛtam .. 9 ..
3.58.d:
तस्माद्दशगुणं सस्यैर्व्रीहिभिर्द्विगुणं ततः ॥
तावदेव तथा पुण्यं होमे सिद्धार्थकैः स्मृतम् ॥ 9 ॥
3.58.m: Ten times that [merit] with grains, twice that with rice; / just as much merit is recorded in offering with white mustard seeds.

3.58.s:
yavaiścaturguṇaṃ tasmāttilairdaśaguṇaṃ tataḥ ..
tāvadeva phalaṃ jñeyaṃ bilvairdaśaguṇaṃ tataḥ .. .. 3.287.10 ..
3.58.d:
यवैश्चतुर्गुणं तस्मात्तिलैर्दशगुणं ततः ॥
तावदेव फलं ज्ञेयं बिल्वैर्दशगुणं ततः ॥ ॥ 3.287.10 ॥
3.58.m: Four times that with barley, ten times that with sesame seeds; / just as much fruit is to be known [with others], and ten times that with bilva fruits.

3.58.s:
padmaiśca tāvadevoktaṃ dadhnā kṣīreṇa ca dvijāḥ ..
paramānnena dharmajñā ghṛtenāṣṭaguṇaṃ tataḥ .. 11 ..
3.58.d:
पद्मैश्च तावदेवोक्तं दध्ना क्षीरेण च द्विजाः ॥
परमान्नेन धर्मज्ञा घृतेनाष्टगुणं ततः ॥ 11 ॥
3.58.m: And just as much is declared with lotuses, with curd and with milk, O twice-born, / and with rice-pudding, O knowers of dharma; eight times that with clarified butter.

3.58.s:
mantreṇoṅkārapūtena svāhāntena vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
svāhāvasāne juhuyāddhyāyanvai mantradevatām .. 12 ..
3.58.d:
मन्त्रेणोङ्कारपूतेन स्वाहान्तेन विचक्षणः ॥
स्वाहावसाने जुहुयाद्ध्यायन्वै मन्त्रदेवताम् ॥ 12 ॥
3.58.m: A discerning person should offer with a mantra purified with the syllable Oṃ and ending in svāhā, / at the conclusion of "svāhā", meditating on the deity of the mantra.

3.58.s:
yayā tvaṅguliparvāṇi pūryante tāvadāhutiḥ ..
aṅguṣṭhamātraṃ sthaulyena vitastiścedhma iṣyate .. 13 ..
3.58.d:
यया त्वङ्गुलिपर्वाणि पूर्यन्ते तावदाहुतिः ॥
अङ्गुष्ठमात्रं स्थौल्येन वितस्तिश्चेध्म इष्यते ॥ 13 ॥
3.58.m: The oblation is as much as fills the joints of the fingers; / and firewood is desired to be a span in length and the measure of a thumb in thickness.

3.58.s:
duḥsvapne ca duriṣṭe ca durnimitte tathaiva ca ..
nāsti homasamantrāṇaṃ tathā pāpavināśanam .. 14 ..
3.58.d:
दुःस्वप्ने च दुरिष्टे च दुर्निमित्ते तथैव च ॥
नास्ति होमसमन्त्राणं तथा पापविनाशनम् ॥ 14 ॥
3.58.m: In bad dreams, in faulty sacrifices, and likewise in ill omens, / there is no destroyer of sin equal to an oblation, nor any [such] protection.

3.58.s:
homena pāpaṃ puruṣo jahāti homena nākaṃ ca tathā prayāti ..
homastu loke duritaṃ samagraṃ vināśayatyeva na saṃśayo'tra .. 15 ..
3.288
haṃsa uvāca ..
daivādhīnā prajāḥ sarvā devāyattamidaṃ jagat ..
sukhaduḥkhe mānuṣāṇāṃ devāyatte tathaiva ca .. 1 ..
devairvihitamaśnanti manuṣyāstu śubhāśubham ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena devapūjāparo bhavet .. 2 ..
devāśca bhaktyā tuṣyanti śraddhayā parayā tathā ..
pūjitāḥ śucinā caiva devāstuṣyanti nānyathā .. 3 ..
devaśuśrūṣayā svargo devaśuśrūṣayā sukham ..
devaśuśrūṣayā rājyaṃ mokṣaṃ cāpyathavāpyate .. 4 ..
devatāḥ kāmayantīha tathā bhaktaṃ janaṃ sadā ..
bhaktānukampino devāḥ paratreha tathā dhruvam .. 5 ..
trāṇaṃ kurvanti bhaktasya dhruvaṃ devā dvijottamāḥ ..
devatoṣādavāpnoti yānkāmānmanasecchati .. 6 ..
3.58.d:
होमेन पापं पुरुषो जहाति होमेन नाकं च तथा प्रयाति ॥
होमस्तु लोके दुरितं समग्रं विनाशयत्येव न संशयोऽत्र ॥ 15 ॥
3.288
हंस उवाच ॥
दैवाधीना प्रजाः सर्वा देवायत्तमिदं जगत् ॥
सुखदुःखे मानुषाणां देवायत्ते तथैव च ॥ 1 ॥
देवैर्विहितमश्नन्ति मनुष्यास्तु शुभाशुभम् ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन देवपूजापरो भवेत् ॥ 2 ॥
देवाश्च भक्त्या तुष्यन्ति श्रद्धया परया तथा ॥
पूजिताः शुचिना चैव देवास्तुष्यन्ति नान्यथा ॥ 3 ॥
देवशुश्रूषया स्वर्गो देवशुश्रूषया सुखम् ॥
देवशुश्रूषया राज्यं मोक्षं चाप्यथवाप्यते ॥ 4 ॥
देवताः कामयन्तीह तथा भक्तं जनं सदा ॥
भक्तानुकम्पिनो देवाः परत्रेह तथा ध्रुवम् ॥ 5 ॥
त्राणं कुर्वन्ति भक्तस्य ध्रुवं देवा द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
देवतोषादवाप्नोति यान्कामान्मनसेच्छति ॥ 6 ॥
3.58.m:
By oblation a person abandons sin; by oblation he likewise goes to heaven; / an oblation indeed destroys all misfortune in the world—there is no doubt of this.
3.288 / Haṃsa said: / All creatures are subject to fate; this world is dependent on the gods; / likewise, the happiness and suffering of human beings are dependent on the gods.
Men experience the good and the bad ordained by the gods; / therefore, with all effort, one should be devoted to the worship of the gods.
And the gods are pleased through devotion, as well as through supreme faith; / worshipped by a pure person, the gods are pleased, and not otherwise.
Through service to the gods, heaven [is attained]; through service to the gods, happiness; / through service to the gods, kingdom or even liberation is attained.
The gods always desire a devoted person in this world; / the gods are surely compassionate to devotees, here and hereafter.
The gods surely protect the devotee, O best of the twice-born; / through the satisfaction of the god, one obtains whatever desires one wishes in one's mind.

3.58.s:
jātaprabhṛti yaṃ devaṃ bhaktyā nityamathārcayeta ..
antakāle tu saṃprāpte so'pi trātā bhaved dhruvam ..7..
kiṃ vā pāpavihīnasya kṣipraṃ tuṣyanti devatāḥ ..
tasmātpāpaṃ na karttavyaṃ nareṇa tridaśāśrayāt .. 8 ..
devāśritānāṃ pāpānāṃ kṣipraṃ pāpaṃ vinaśyati ..
natveva pātakaṃ karma vṛthā teṣāṃ prajāyate .. 9 ..
tathā bahu phalaṃ loke kathitaṃ tridaśāśrayam ..
sarvānsamarcayeddevānekaṃ vā devamāśrayet .. 3.288.10 ..
devārcāṃ śraddhayā kṛtvā dhruvaṃ tallokamāpnuyāt ..
kṛtvā devagṛhaṃ viprā narastallokamāpnuyāt .. 11 ..
paramāṇūni yāvanti bhavanti suraveśmanaḥ ..
tāvato'bdānavāpnoti tallokānnātra saṃśayaḥ .. 12 ..
yāvadvāraṃ karotīha devaveśma sudhāsitam ..
janmāntarāṇi tāvanti yaśasā sa virājate .. 13 ..
3.58.d:
जातप्रभृति यं देवं भक्त्या नित्यमथार्चयेत ॥
अन्तकाले तु संप्राप्ते सोऽपि त्राता भवेद् ध्रुवम् ॥7॥
किं वा पापविहीनस्य क्षिप्रं तुष्यन्ति देवताः ॥
तस्मात्पापं न कर्त्तव्यं नरेण त्रिदशाश्रयात् ॥ 8 ॥
देवाश्रितानां पापानां क्षिप्रं पापं विनश्यति ॥
नत्वेव पातकं कर्म वृथा तेषां प्रजायते ॥ 9 ॥
तथा बहु फलं लोके कथितं त्रिदशाश्रयम् ॥
सर्वान्समर्चयेद्देवानेकं वा देवमाश्रयेत् ॥ 3.288.10 ॥
देवार्चां श्रद्धया कृत्वा ध्रुवं तल्लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥
कृत्वा देवगृहं विप्रा नरस्तल्लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥ 11 ॥
परमाणूनि यावन्ति भवन्ति सुरवेश्मनः ॥
तावतोऽब्दानवाप्नोति तल्लोकान्नात्र संशयः ॥ 12 ॥
यावद्वारं करोतीह देववेश्म सुधासितम् ॥
जन्मान्तराणि तावन्ति यशसा स विराजते ॥ 13 ॥
3.58.m:
Whatever god one should constantly worship with devotion from birth onward, / when the time of death arrives, that [god] surely becomes one's savior.
Or rather, the deities are swiftly pleased with one free from sin; / therefore a man should not commit sin, taking refuge in the gods.
The sin of sinners who have taken refuge in a god is swiftly destroyed; / indeed, sinful action does not arise in vain for them.
Thus taking refuge in the gods is proclaimed in the world to bear great fruit. / One should worship all the gods, or take refuge in a single god.
Having performed the worship of a god with faith, one surely attains that deity's world; / having built a house for a god, O brahmins, a man attains that deity's world.
As many atoms as there are in the abode of the god, / for so many years he attains that deity's world; of this there is no doubt.
As many times as he makes the house of the god whitewashed with mortar in this world, / for so many future births he shines with fame.

3.58.s:
pratipādya tathā bhaktyā dhvajaṃ tridaśaveśmani ..
nirṇudatyāśu pāpāni mahāpātakajānyapi .. 14 ..
citrakarma tathā kṛtvā gandharvai saha modate ..
devamālyāpanayanādgodānaphalamāpnuyāt. .. 15 ..
3.58.d:
प्रतिपाद्य तथा भक्त्या ध्वजं त्रिदशवेश्मनि ॥
निर्णुदत्याशु पापानि महापातकजान्यपि ॥ 14 ॥
चित्रकर्म तथा कृत्वा गन्धर्वै सह मोदते ॥
देवमाल्यापनयनाद्गोदानफलमाप्नुयात्॥। 15 ॥
3.58.m:
Likewise, dedicating a banner at the house of the gods with devotion, / one quickly dispels sins, even those born of heinous crimes.
Likewise, having made a painting, he rejoices with the gandharvas; / from removing withered garlands from a god, one obtains the fruit of giving a cow.

3.58.s:
pāpairvimucyate sarvaiḥ prokṣaṇāddevaveśmanaḥ ..
sammārjanāttathā pāpaṃ vyapohati na saṃśayaḥ .. 16 ..
3.58.d:
पापैर्विमुच्यते सर्वैः प्रोक्षणाद्देववेश्मनः ॥
सम्मार्जनात्तथा पापं व्यपोहति न संशयः ॥ 16 ॥
3.58.m: One is freed from all sins by sprinkling the house of a god; / likewise, by sweeping it, one removes sin without doubt.

3.58.s:
kāmānabhīṣṭānāpnoti devaveśmopalepanāt ..
sudhārekhānvitaṃ kṛtvā maryādāṃ nātivartate .. 17 ..
3.58.d:
कामानभीष्टानाप्नोति देववेश्मोपलेपनात् ॥
सुधारेखान्वितं कृत्वा मर्यादां नातिवर्तते ॥ 17 ॥
3.58.m: One obtains desired wishes by smearing the house of a god; / having made it marked with lines of mortar, one does not exceed proper limits.

3.58.s:
varṇakaiścitritaṃ kṛtvā saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
gandharvatvamavāpnoti gandhairabhyukṣya mānavāḥ .. 18 ..
3.58.d:
वर्णकैश्चित्रितं कृत्वा सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
गन्धर्वत्वमवाप्नोति गन्धैरभ्युक्ष्य मानवाः ॥ 18 ॥
3.58.m: Having decorated it with pigments, one obtains great good fortune; / sprinkling it with perfumes, men attain gandharva-hood.

3.58.s:
puṣpairvikiraṇaṃ kṛtvā rūpavānabhijāyate ..
abhyajya devapratimāṃ sarvaduḥkhairvimucyate .. 19 ..
3.58.d:
पुष्पैर्विकिरणं कृत्वा रूपवानभिजायते ॥
अभ्यज्य देवप्रतिमां सर्वदुःखैर्विमुच्यते ॥ 19 ॥
3.58.m: Scattering [it] with flowers, one is born handsome; / by anointing the image of a god, one is freed from all sufferings.

3.58.s:
virūkṣayitvā tāmeva pāpebhyo vipramucyate ..
oṣadhībhistathā snāpya nāsatyaiḥ saha modate .. 3.288.20 ..
3.58.d:
विरूक्षयित्वा तामेव पापेभ्यो विप्रमुच्यते ॥
ओषधीभिस्तथा स्नाप्य नासत्यैः सह मोदते ॥ 3.288.20 ॥
3.58.m: Removing the unguents from it, one is completely freed from sins; / bathing [it] with herbs, he rejoices with the Nāsatyas.

3.58.s:
loke prajāpateryāti vedaiḥ saṃsnāpya devatām ...
puṣpodakena snapanātsaubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute .. 21 ..
3.58.d:
लोके प्रजापतेर्याति वेदैः संस्नाप्य देवताम् ॥।
पुष्पोदकेन स्नपनात्सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥ 21 ॥
3.58.m: Bathing the deity with the Vedas, he goes to the world of Prajāpati; / by bathing [the deity] with flower-scented water, one enjoys great good fortune.

3.58.s:
phalodakena saṃsnāpya saphalāṃ vindate kriyām ..
nāgavallījalaiḥ snāpya nāgalokaṃ sa gacchati .. 22 ..
3.58.d:
फलोदकेन संस्नाप्य सफलां विन्दते क्रियाम् ॥
नागवल्लीजलैः स्नाप्य नागलोकं स गच्छति ॥ 22 ॥
3.58.m: Bathing [the deity] with fruit-water, one attains fruitful action; / bathing [the deity] with betel-leaf water, he goes to the world of the nāgas.

3.58.s:
ratnodakena snapanāddhānadaṃ lokamāpnuyāt ..
gandhodakena mukhyena gandharvaiḥ saha modate .. 23 ..
3.58.d:
रत्नोदकेन स्नपनाद्धानदं लोकमाप्नुयात् ॥
गन्धोदकेन मुख्येन गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥ 23 ॥
3.58.m: By bathing [the deity] with water of gems, one attains the world of the Wealth-Giver; / with the foremost perfumed water, he rejoices with the gandharvas.

3.58.s:
tīrthodakena puṇyena svargalokamavāpnuyāt ..
tathānulipya gandhaiśca śakraloke mahīyate .. 24 ..
3.58.d:
तीर्थोदकेन पुण्येन स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
तथानुलिप्य गन्धैश्च शक्रलोके महीयते ॥ 24 ॥
3.58.m: With auspicious water from sacred pilgrimage places, one attains the heavenly world; / and having anointed [the deity] with perfumes, he is exalted in Śakra's world.

3.58.s:
vibhūṣaṇapradānena rājā bhavati bhūtale ..
rājaliṅgapradānena rājā bhavati hi kṣitau .. 25 ..
3.58.d:
विभूषणप्रदानेन राजा भवति भूतले ॥
राजलिङ्गप्रदानेन राजा भवति हि क्षितौ ॥ 25 ॥
3.58.m: By giving ornaments, one becomes a king on the earth; / by giving the insignia of royalty, one indeed becomes a king on earth.

3.58.s:
vastradānena loke'sminsuveśastvabhijāyate ..
deve mālyapradānena parā lakṣmīṃ samaśnute .. 26 ..
3.58.d:
वस्त्रदानेन लोकेऽस्मिन्सुवेशस्त्वभिजायते ॥
देवे माल्यप्रदानेन परा लक्ष्मीं समश्नुते ॥ 26 ॥
3.58.m: By giving cloth, one is born beautifully dressed in this world; / by giving a garland to a god, one enjoys supreme prosperity.

3.58.s:
dhūpapradānena tathā gatimagryāmavāpnuyāt ..
dīpadānena cakṣuṣmānprakāśaścaiva jāyate .. 27 ..
3.58.d:
धूपप्रदानेन तथा गतिमग्र्यामवाप्नुयात् ॥
दीपदानेन चक्षुष्मान्प्रकाशश्चैव जायते ॥ 27 ॥
3.58.m: Likewise, by giving incense, one attains the highest path; / by giving a lamp, one becomes endowed with vision and luminous.

3.58.s:
ūrdhvāṃ gatimavāpnoti sarvatra ca tathāgryatām ..
devatābhyastathā viprā nivedyānnamatandritaḥ .. 28 ..
3.58.d:
ऊर्ध्वां गतिमवाप्नोति सर्वत्र च तथाग्र्यताम् ॥
देवताभ्यस्तथा विप्रा निवेद्यान्नमतन्द्रितः ॥ 28 ॥
3.58.m: He attains an upward path, and supreme status everywhere; / and unweariedly offering food to deities, O brahmins,

3.58.s:
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute ..
paritoṣamathāyāti devatā balikarmaṇā .. 29 ..
3.58.d:
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ॥
परितोषमथायाति देवता बलिकर्मणा ॥ 29 ॥
3.58.m: he enjoys the fruit of a sacrifice replete with all desires; / and a deity attains satisfaction through the ritual offering of food.

3.58.s:
tāstuṣṭāstarpayanyenaṃ sarvakāmasamṛddhibhiḥ ..
hṛdyapānapradānena tṛptimāpnoti śāśvatīm .. 3.288.30 ..
3.58.d:
तास्तुष्टास्तर्पयन्येनं सर्वकामसमृद्धिभिः ॥
हृद्यपानप्रदानेन तृप्तिमाप्नोति शाश्वतीम् ॥ 3.288.30 ॥
3.58.m: Pleased, they satisfy him with the fulfillments of all desires; / by offering delightful drinks, one attains everlasting satisfaction.

3.58.s:
devatānāṃ namaskārātkiñcitpāpaṃ praṇaśyati ..
tathaivābhyadhikaṃ pāpaṃ praṇipātena naśyati .. 31 ..
3.58.d:
देवतानां नमस्कारात्किञ्चित्पापं प्रणश्यति ॥
तथैवाभ्यधिकं पापं प्रणिपातेन नश्यति ॥ 31 ॥
3.58.m: From bowing to deities, some sin is destroyed; / likewise, greater sin is destroyed by prostration.

3.58.s:
tato'pyabhyadhikaṃ kiñcitkṛtvā deve pradakṣiṇām ..
stutikriyā devatānāṃ sarvakāmaphalapradā .. 32 ...
3.58.d:
ततोऽप्यभ्यधिकं किञ्चित्कृत्वा देवे प्रदक्षिणाम् ॥
स्तुतिक्रिया देवतानां सर्वकामफलप्रदा ॥ 32 ॥।
3.58.m: Something still greater than that [is gained] by circumambulating a god; / the act of praising deities bestows the fruit of all desires.

3.58.s:
gītena devatāstoṣamupayānti dvijottamāḥ ..
tathā vādyena nṛtyena puruṣasya viśeṣataḥ ..33 ..
3.58.d:
गीतेन देवतास्तोषमुपयान्ति द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
तथा वाद्येन नृत्येन पुरुषस्य विशेषतः ॥33 ॥
3.58.m: O best of the twice-born, the deities attain satisfaction through song, / and especially through instrumental music and dance offered by a man.

3.58.s:
nṛttaṃ gītaṃ tathā vādyaṃ svayamācarate dvijā ..
devasālokyamāpnoti puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ .. 34 ..
3.58.d:
नृत्तं गीतं तथा वाद्यं स्वयमाचरते द्विजा ॥
देवसालोक्यमाप्नोति पुरुषस्य विपश्चितः ॥ 34 ॥
3.58.m: If a wise man himself performs dance, song, / and instrumental music, O twice-born, he attains co-residence with the god.

3.58.s:
vācanāditihāsānāṃ pāpamokṣamavāpnuyāt ..
mūlyena kārayedgītaṃ gandharvatvamathāpnuyāt .. 35 ..
3.58.d:
वाचनादितिहासानां पापमोक्षमवाप्नुयात् ॥
मूल्येन कारयेद्गीतं गन्धर्वत्वमथाप्नुयात् ॥ 35 ॥
3.58.m: From the recitation of historical epics, one attains release from sin; / if one arranges song by paying a price, one attains gandharva-hood.

3.58.s:
vādyaṃ dattvātha dharmajñaṃ vasūnāṃ lokamaśnute ..
nṛttena lokamāpnoti śaṅkarasya mahātmanaḥ .. 36 ..
3.58.d:
वाद्यं दत्त्वाथ धर्मज्ञं वसूनां लोकमश्नुते ॥
नृत्तेन लोकमाप्नोति शङ्करस्य महात्मनः ॥ 36 ॥
3.58.m: Providing instrumental music, one who knows dharma enjoys the world of the Vasus; / through dance, one attains the world of the great-souled Śaṅkara.

3.58.s:
itihāsapradānena buddhimāñjāyate naraḥ ..
āhutiṃ devamuddiśya yo dadāti hutāśane .. 37 ..
3.58.d:
इतिहासप्रदानेन बुद्धिमाञ्जायते नरः ॥
आहुतिं देवमुद्दिश्य यो ददाति हुताशने ॥ 37 ॥
3.58.m: By presenting historical epics, a man becomes intelligent. / Whoever offers an oblation in the sacrificial fire dedicated to a god,

3.58.s:
sa devastarpayatyenaṃ kāmairvā tena tarpitaḥ ..
devamuddiśya viprāṇāṃ yo dadātīha bhojanam .. 38 ..
3.58.d:
स देवस्तर्पयत्येनं कामैर्वा तेन तर्पितः ॥
देवमुद्दिश्य विप्राणां यो ददातीह भोजनम् ॥ 38 ॥
3.58.m: that god, satisfied by him, satisfies him with desired things. / Whoever in this world offers food to brahmins dedicated to a god,

3.58.s:
sa devaḥ prītimānasya kāmāniṣṭānprayacchati ..
devamuddiśya yatkiñcidbrāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradīyate ..39..
3.58.d:
स देवः प्रीतिमानस्य कामानिष्टान्प्रयच्छति ॥
देवमुद्दिश्य यत्किञ्चिद्ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदीयते ॥39॥
3.58.m: that god, being pleased with him, bestows his cherished desires. / Whatever is given to brahmins dedicated to a god,

3.58.s:
tadeva prāpyate loke prasanne tridaśe bahu ..
yānaṃ śayyāsanaṃ chatraṃ pāduke cāpyupānahau .. 3.288.40 ..
3.58.d:
तदेव प्राप्यते लोके प्रसन्ने त्रिदशे बहु ॥
यानं शय्यासनं छत्रं पादुके चाप्युपानहौ ॥ 3.288.40 ॥
3.58.m: that very thing is obtained abundantly in the world when the god is pleased: / a carriage, a bed, a seat, an umbrella, sandals, and shoes.

3.58.s:
vāhanaṃ gāṃ ca dharmajñāstridaśabhyo dadāti yaḥ ..
ekaikasmādavāpnoti vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ naraḥ .. 41 ..
3.58.d:
वाहनं गां च धर्मज्ञास्त्रिदशभ्यो ददाति यः ॥
एकैकस्मादवाप्नोति वह्निष्टोमफलं नरः ॥ 41 ॥
3.58.m: The man who gives a mount or a cow to the gods, O knowers of dharma, / obtains the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice from each one.

3.58.s:
dattvā phalāni devebhyaḥ saphalāṃ vindate kriyām ..
nivedya sasyāni tathā gatimāpnotyanuttamām .. 42 ..
3.58.d:
दत्त्वा फलानि देवेभ्यः सफलां विन्दते क्रियाम् ॥
निवेद्य सस्यानि तथा गतिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥ 42 ॥
3.58.m: Having given fruits to the gods, one finds one's work fruitful; / likewise, having offered crops, one attains an unsurpassed state.

3.58.s:
naiti devastathā prītiṃ dānairnṛtyaistathā phalaiḥ ..
prītimeti yathā viprāḥ svāśritānāntu pūjanaiḥ .. 43 ..
3.58.d:
नैति देवस्तथा प्रीतिं दानैर्नृत्यैस्तथा फलैः ॥
प्रीतिमेति यथा विप्राः स्वाश्रितानान्तु पूजनैः ॥ 43 ॥
3.58.m: A god does not attain such pleasure through gifts, through dances, or through fruits, / as he attains pleasure, O brahmins, through the worship of those who take refuge in him.

3.58.s:
devatā naiva tuṣyanti dānena bahudhā dvijāḥ ..
yathā bhaktyā tu tuṣyanti tasmādbhaktiṃ samāśrayet .. 44 ..
3.58.d:
देवता नैव तुष्यन्ति दानेन बहुधा द्विजाः ॥
यथा भक्त्या तु तुष्यन्ति तस्माद्भक्तिं समाश्रयेत् ॥ 44 ॥
3.58.m: Deities are not so greatly pleased by giving, O twice-born, / as they are pleased through devotion; therefore one should resort to devotion.

3.58.s:
ghṛtapūrṇāni pātrāṇi dattvā śrāddhe tathā naraḥ ..
dīrghaṃ jīvitamāpnoti na rogaiścābhibhūyate .. 45 ..
3.58.d:
घृतपूर्णानि पात्राणि दत्त्वा श्राद्धे तथा नरः ॥
दीर्घं जीवितमाप्नोति न रोगैश्चाभिभूयते ॥ 45 ॥
3.58.m: Having given vessels full of clarified butter in a ancestral rite, a man / attains a long life and is not overcome by diseases.

3.58.s:
madhupūrṇāni pātrāṇi dattvā saubhāgyamāpnuyāt ..
yathākathañcitpātrāṇāṃ dānādbhavati sattamāḥ ..46..
3.58.d:
मधुपूर्णानि पात्राणि दत्त्वा सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
यथाकथञ्चित्पात्राणां दानाद्भवति सत्तमाः ॥46॥
3.58.m: Having given vessels full of honey, one obtains good fortune. / From the gift of vessels in any manner whatsoever, O best of men,

3.58.s:
pātraṃ nu sarvakāmānāṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
puṣpavṛkṣapradānena gṛhamāpnoti mānavaḥ .. 47 ..
3.58.d:
पात्रं नु सर्वकामानां नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
पुष्पवृक्षप्रदानेन गृहमाप्नोति मानवः ॥ 47 ॥
3.58.m: one becomes a vessel indeed for all desired things; no doubt should be entertained here. / By giving flowering trees, a man obtains a home.

3.58.s:
phalavṛkṣapradānena grāmasyādhipatirbhavet ..
gṛhapradānāddhavati kheṭakādhipatistathā .. 48 ..
3.58.d:
फलवृक्षप्रदानेन ग्रामस्याधिपतिर्भवेत् ॥
गृहप्रदानाद्धवति खेटकाधिपतिस्तथा ॥ 48 ॥
3.58.m: By giving fruit-bearing trees, one becomes the lord of a village; / likewise, by giving a house, one becomes the lord of an agricultural town.

3.58.s:
gṛhaṃ śayyāsanopetaṃ yānavāhanasaṃyutam ..
dhanadhānyayutaṃ sphītaṃ dāsīdāsasamākulam .. 49 ..
3.58.d:
गृहं शय्यासनोपेतं यानवाहनसंयुतम् ॥
धनधान्ययुतं स्फीतं दासीदाससमाकुलम् ॥ 49 ॥
3.58.m: A house furnished with beds and seats, supplied with vehicles and mounts, / filled with wealth and grain, abundant, crowded with female and male slaves,

3.58.s:
sarvakāmayutaṃ ramyaṃ pradāya śrāddhakarmaṇi ..
svargalokātparibhraṣṭo rājā bhavati pārthivaḥ .. 3.288.50 ..
3.58.d:
सर्वकामयुतं रम्यं प्रदाय श्राद्धकर्मणि ॥
स्वर्गलोकात्परिभ्रष्टो राजा भवति पार्थिवः ॥ 3.288.50 ॥
3.58.m: equipped with all desirable things, beautiful—having given it in the rite of a śrāddha, / having descended from heaven, he becomes an earthly king.

3.58.s:
pitṝnuddiśya yaddānaṃ kiñcideva prayacchati..
tasyābhyadhikamāpnoti puṇyaṃ teṣāṃ prasādataḥ .. 51 ..
3.58.d:
पितॄनुद्दिश्य यद्दानं किञ्चिदेव प्रयच्छति॥
तस्याभ्यधिकमाप्नोति पुण्यं तेषां प्रसादतः ॥ 51 ॥
3.58.m: Whatever gift one offers, even a little, intended for the ancestors, / through their grace he obtains even greater merit than that.

3.58.s:
tasmācchrāddhāni kāryāṇi tīrtheṣvāyataneṣu ca ..
dānāni caiva deyāni pitṝnuddiśya śaktitaḥ..52..
3.58.d:
तस्माच्छ्राद्धानि कार्याणि तीर्थेष्वायतनेषु च ॥
दानानि चैव देयानि पितॄनुद्दिश्य शक्तितः॥52॥
3.58.m: Therefore śrāddhas are to be performed at sacred tirthas and in temples, / and gifts are certainly to be given for the ancestors according to one's capacity.

3.58.s:
śrāddheṣu puṣṭiṃ manujā labhante śrāddhena viprāstridive ca vāsaḥ..
śrāddhaṃ prayatnena tataśca kuryātsvakalpasūtrābhihitaṃ yathāvat ..53..
3.289
haṃsa uvāca ..
śūdrāṇāṃ daivataṃ vaiśyā vaiśyānāṃ kṣatriyāstathā ..
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca teṣāmapi hutāśanaḥ .. 1 ..
gurudevo brahmacārī nāryaśca patidevatāḥ ..
gṛhastho'tithidaivatyastasmāttaṃ pūjayetsadā .. 2 ..
vaiśvadevaṃ gṛhe kṛtvā sāyaṃ prātaḥ samāhitaḥ ..
piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ kṛtvā bhikṣāṃ dattvā tu bhikṣave.. ..
satkṛtya bhikṣādānena godānaphalamāpnuyāt ..
śvabhyaśca śvapacebhyaśca vayobhyaścāvapedbhuvi .. 4 ..
gṛhasthamupajīvanti prajāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ ..
gṛhasthaḥ poṣaṇaṃ kuryānmṛtānāṃ jīvatāmapi .. 5 ..
poṣaṇānnityameveha tena svarge mahīyate ..
kīṭaḥ pataṅgaḥ patitaḥ śatravo dvijapuṅgavāḥ..6..
3.58.d:
श्राद्धेषु पुष्टिं मनुजा लभन्ते श्राद्धेन विप्रास्त्रिदिवे च वासः॥
श्राद्धं प्रयत्नेन ततश्च कुर्यात्स्वकल्पसूत्राभिहितं यथावत् ॥53॥
3.289
हंस उवाच ॥
शूद्राणां दैवतं वैश्या वैश्यानां क्षत्रियास्तथा ॥
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रियाणां च तेषामपि हुताशनः ॥ 1 ॥
गुरुदेवो ब्रह्मचारी नार्यश्च पतिदेवताः ॥
गृहस्थोऽतिथिदैवत्यस्तस्मात्तं पूजयेत्सदा ॥ 2 ॥
वैश्वदेवं गृहे कृत्वा सायं प्रातः समाहितः ॥
पिण्डनिर्वपणं कृत्वा भिक्षां दत्त्वा तु भिक्षवे॥ ॥
सत्कृत्य भिक्षादानेन गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥
श्वभ्यश्च श्वपचेभ्यश्च वयोभ्यश्चावपेद्भुवि ॥ 4 ॥
गृहस्थमुपजीवन्ति प्रजाः स्थावरजङ्गमाः ॥
गृहस्थः पोषणं कुर्यान्मृतानां जीवतामपि ॥ 5 ॥
पोषणान्नित्यमेवेह तेन स्वर्गे महीयते ॥
कीटः पतङ्गः पतितः शत्रवो द्विजपुङ्गवाः॥6॥
3.58.m:
In śrāddhas men attain nourishment; through a śrāddha the wise attain residence in heaven. / Therefore, one should diligently perform the śrāddha duly prescribed by one's own ritual manual.
3.289
Haṃsa said:
Vaiśyas are the deity of śūdras, and kṣatriyas are [the deity] of vaiśyas; / brahmins are [the deity] of kṣatriyas, and the fire-god is also [the deity] of those [brahmins].
The celibate student has the teacher as deity, and women have the husband as deity; / the householder has the guest as deity; therefore, he should always honour him.
Having performed the vaiśvadeva rite in the home evening and morning with concentrated mind, / having offered the rice balls, and having given alms to an ascetic, / by respectfully giving alms, he obtains the fruit of giving a cow; / and he should scatter food on the ground for dogs, dog-cookers, and birds.
Immobile and mobile creatures depend on the householder for life; / the householder should sustain both the dead and the living.
Because he continually sustains [them] here, he is exalted in heaven; / worms, insects, fallen outcasts, enemies, and foremost of the twice-born—

3.58.s:
gṛhiṇā nāvamantavyā vaiśvadeve hyupasthite ..
atithiṃ pūjayedyatnāgṛhastho gṛhamāgatam .. 7 ..

pādaśaucena tasyātha śrāntasaṃvāhanena ca .. 9 ..

3.58.d:
गृहिणा नावमन्तव्या वैश्वदेवे ह्युपस्थिते ॥
अतिथिं पूजयेद्यत्नागृहस्थो गृहमागतम् ॥ 7 ॥
उत्थायास्य व्रजन्पूर्वे गोदानफलमाप्नुयात् ॥
आसनं च तथा दत्त्वा स्थानलाभं नरोत्तमः ॥ 8 ॥
कृत्वा च कुशल प्रश्नं बुद्धिमाञ्जायते नरः ॥
पादशौचेन तस्याथ श्रान्तसंवाहनेन च ॥ 9 ॥
वीजनाच्चामरेणापि तालवृन्तेन वीजनात् ॥
पादाभ्यङ्गप्रदानेन दीपदानेन वाप्यथ ॥ 3.289.10 ॥
रात्रौ शयनदानेन तथा संवाहनेन च ॥
एकैकस्मादवाप्नोति गोदानफलमुत्तमम् ॥ 11 ॥
उपास्यैनं कथाभिश्च यशसा योगमाप्नुयात् ॥
संश्राव्य चेतिहासानि तथैनं च तदिच्छया ॥ 12 ॥
नाकलोकमवाप्नोति गीतनृत्योत्सवादिभिः ॥
पूजयित्वा तथाप्नोति गन्धर्वत्वमसंशयम् ॥ 13 ॥
प्रतिश्रयप्रदानेन सर्वान्कामान्समश्नुते ॥
मृदं च दन्तकाष्ठं च दत्त्वा शौचोदकं तथा ॥ 14 ॥
3.58.m:
these are not to be disregarded by the householder when the vaiśvadeva has arrived. / The householder should diligently honour the guest who has come to his home.
By standing up and advancing before him, he attains the fruit of giving a cow; / and by offering a seat, that best of men attains a station.
And by inquiring after his well-being, a man becomes intelligent; / then, by washing his feet and massaging his weary [limbs],
by fanning him with a chowrie or by fanning him with a palm leaf, / by offering anointment for his feet, or by offering a lamp,
by providing a bed at night, and likewise by massaging him— / from each single one, he obtains the highest fruit of giving a cow.
By attending upon him with stories, he attains union with fame; / and by reciting historical narratives to him according to his desire,
he attains the heavenly world; with song, dance, festivities, and the like, / having honoured him, he undoubtedly attains the state of a gandharva.
By granting shelter, he enjoys all desired things; / and having offered earth, a tooth-stick, and water for cleansing,

3.58.s:
kāle yathāsukhaṃ dattvā saubhāgyaṃ mahadāpnuyāt ..
pratāpya cainaṃ śītārtaṃ sarvatra sukhamaśnute .. 15 ..
abhyaṅgapūrvakaṃ dattvā tasya snānamatandritaḥ ..
ārogyarūpalāvaṇyadhanadhānyamupāśnute .. 16 ..
dattvā sakalamukhyāni snānāni dvijasattamāḥ ..
nāsatyalokamāpnoti nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..17 ..
sugandhīni tathā dattvā gandharvaiḥ saha modate ..
kaṃkaṇasya pradānena saubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute .. 18 ..
atithisnāpanātpuṇyaṃ daśagodānajaṃ bhavet ..
kimicchukena saṃyojya vājapeyaphalaṃ labhet .. 19 ..
svecchitaṃ ca pradāyāsya tadevākṣayamaśnute ..
sarvaśaktyā narastasmādatithiṃ pūjayetsadā .. 3.289.20 ..
tṛpto'tithiryatpuruṣasya kiñcidvicintayatyeva mahānubhāvaḥ ..
tatsarvamāpnotyacireṇa tasmātpūjyo'tithirdharmapareṇa nityam .. 21 ..
3.58.d:
काले यथासुखं दत्त्वा सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
प्रताप्य चैनं शीतार्तं सर्वत्र सुखमश्नुते ॥ 15 ॥
अभ्यङ्गपूर्वकं दत्त्वा तस्य स्नानमतन्द्रितः ॥
आरोग्यरूपलावण्यधनधान्यमुपाश्नुते ॥ 16 ॥
दत्त्वा सकलमुख्यानि स्नानानि द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
नासत्यलोकमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥17 ॥
सुगन्धीनि तथा दत्त्वा गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते ॥
कंकणस्य प्रदानेन सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥ 18 ॥
अतिथिस्नापनात्पुण्यं दशगोदानजं भवेत् ॥
किमिच्छुकेन संयोज्य वाजपेयफलं लभेत् ॥ 19 ॥
स्वेच्छितं च प्रदायास्य तदेवाक्षयमश्नुते ॥
सर्वशक्त्या नरस्तस्मादतिथिं पूजयेत्सदा ॥ 3.289.20 ॥
तृप्तोऽतिथिर्यत्पुरुषस्य किञ्चिद्विचिन्तयत्येव महानुभावः ॥
तत्सर्वमाप्नोत्यचिरेण तस्मात्पूज्योऽतिथिर्धर्मपरेण नित्यम् ॥ 21 ॥
3.58.m:
having provided it at the proper time to his comfort, he attains great good fortune; / and by warming him when afflicted by cold, he enjoys comfort everywhere.
Having unweariedly provided him a bath preceded by an oil-rub, / he enjoys health, beauty, grace, wealth, and grain.
Having provided all kinds of principal baths, O best of the twice-born, / he attains the world of the Nāsatya twins; on this point no doubt should be made.
Likewise, having given fragrant perfumes, he rejoices with the gandharvas; / by the gift of a bracelet, he enjoys great good fortune.
From bathing a guest, the merit produced is equal to the gift of ten cows; / by gratifying him with whatever he desires, one obtains the fruit of a Vājapeya sacrifice.
And having given him whatever he desires, he enjoys that very thing inexhaustibly; / therefore, with all his strength, a man should always honour the guest.
Whatever that noble [guest], being satisfied, wishes for a man, / he attains all that before long; therefore, the guest must always be worshipped by one devoted to dharma.

brāhmaṇā daivataṃ bhūmau brāhmaṇā divi daivatam ..

brāhmaṇebhyaḥ samutpannā devāḥ pūrvamiti śrutiḥ ..
brāhmaṇebhyo jagatsarvaṃ tasmātpūjyatamāḥ sadā .. 3 ..

3.58.d:
3.290
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
ब्राह्मणा दैवतं भूमौ ब्राह्मणा दिवि दैवतम् ॥
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः परं नास्ति भूतं किंञ्चिज्जगत्त्रये ॥ 1 ॥
अदैवं दैवतं कुर्युः कुर्युर्दैवमदैवतम् ॥
ब्राह्मणा हि महाभागाः पूज्यन्ते सततं द्विजाः ॥ 2 ॥
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः समुत्पन्ना देवाः पूर्वमिति श्रुतिः ॥
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो जगत्सर्वं तस्मात्पूज्यतमाः सदा ॥ 3 ॥
एषामश्नन्ति वक्त्रेण देवताः पितरस्तथा ॥
ऋषयश्च महाभागाः किम्भूतमधिकं ततः ॥ 4 ॥
यदेव मनुजो भक्त्या ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रयच्छति ॥
तदेवाप्नोति धर्मज्ञा बहु जन्मनिजन्मनि ॥ 5 ॥
तालवृन्तानिलेनैवं श्रान्तसंवाहनेन च ॥
उन्मार्जनेन गात्राणां तथाप्यञ्जनकर्मणा ॥ 6 ॥
पादशौचप्रदानेन पादयोः शौचनेन च ॥
परिचर्यया यथाकाममेकेनैव द्विजोत्तमाः ॥ 7 ॥
3.58.m:
3.290
Haṃsa said:
Brahmins are the deity on earth; brahmins are the deity in heaven; / there is no being whatever higher than brahmins in the three worlds.
They can make a non-deity into a deity; they can make a deity into a non-deity; / for brahmins are exalted, twice-born [beings who] are constantly worshipped.
From brahmins the gods were originally born, so says sacred tradition; / from brahmins comes the entire world; therefore, they are always most worthy of worship.
Through their mouth deities eat, and likewise the ancestors / and the exalted sages; what being is greater than that?
Whatever a man gives with devotion to brahmins, / that very thing he obtains in abundance, O knowers of dharma, birth after birth.
Even with wind from a palm-leaf fan, and by massaging weary [limbs], / by wiping limbs clean, and likewise by the act of applying collyrium,
by offering washing for the feet, and by cleansing of both feet, / by personal service as desired—through just a single one, O best of the twice-born,

3.58.s:
agniṣṭomamavāpnoti svargalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
brāhmaṇājñāṃ śubhāṃ kṛtvā nākaloke mahīyate ..8..
yadbrāhmaṇāstuṣṭatamā vadanti taddevatāḥ pratyabhinandayanti ..
tuṣṭeṣu tuṣṭāḥ satataṃ bhavanti pratyakṣadeveṣu parokṣadevāḥ..9..
3.58.d:
अग्निष्टोममवाप्नोति स्वर्गलोकं च गच्छति ॥
ब्राह्मणाज्ञां शुभां कृत्वा नाकलोके महीयते ॥8॥
यद्ब्राह्मणास्तुष्टतमा वदन्ति तद्देवताः प्रत्यभिनन्दयन्ति ॥
तुष्टेषु तुष्टाः सततं भवन्ति प्रत्यक्षदेवेषु परोक्षदेवाः॥9॥
3.58.m:
he attains the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice and goes to the heavenly world; / having carried out an auspicious command of a brahmin, he is exalted in the heavenly world.
Whatever brahmins, when fully pleased, speak, the deities applaud; / when the visible gods are pleased, the invisible gods are constantly pleased.

3.59.s:
3.291
.. haṃsa uvāca ..
gāvaḥ pavitrā maṅgalyā goṣu lokāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ ..
yathā devā yathā vedā brāhmaṇāśca yathā dvijāḥ .. 1 ..
3.59.d:
3.291
॥ हंस उवाच ॥
गावः पवित्रा मङ्गल्या गोषु लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥
यथा देवा यथा वेदा ब्राह्मणाश्च यथा द्विजाः ॥ 1 ॥
3.59.m:
3.291
Haṃsa said:
Cows are pure and auspicious; the worlds are established in cows; / just as the gods, just as the Vedas, and just as brahmins are twice-born,

3.59.s:
tathā gāvo vinirdiṣṭāḥ sarvalokasukhāvahāḥ ..
ekaikaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ jñeyaṃ tayoryajñaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ .. 2 ..
3.59.d:
तथा गावो विनिर्दिष्टाः सर्वलोकसुखावहाः ॥
एकैकं ब्राह्मणं ज्ञेयं तयोर्यज्ञः प्रतिष्ठितः ॥ 2 ॥
3.59.m: so cows are declared to bring happiness to all the worlds; / each single one is to be known as a brahmin; in the two of them sacrifice is established.

3.59.s:
vipreṣu mantrāstiṣṭhanti goṣu santiṣṭhate haviḥ ..
gavāṃ dānaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhā duṣkṛtānyapakarṣati ..3..
3.59.d:
विप्रेषु मन्त्रास्तिष्ठन्ति गोषु सन्तिष्ठते हविः ॥
गवां दानं द्विजश्रेष्ठा दुष्कृतान्यपकर्षति ॥3॥
3.59.m: Mantras reside in the wise, and the oblation resides in cows; / the gift of cows, O best of the twice-born, removes evil deeds.

3.59.s:
gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi sarpiśca pañcamam ..
pavitrametannirdiṣṭaṃ narāṇāṃ śodhanaṃ param .. 4 ..
3.59.d:
गोमूत्रं गोमयं क्षीरं दधि सर्पिश्च पञ्चमम् ॥
पवित्रमेतन्निर्दिष्टं नराणां शोधनं परम् ॥ 4 ॥
3.59.m:
Cow urine, cow dung, milk, curd, and fifth, clarified butter:
this is declared holy, the supreme purifier of human beings.

3.59.s:
maṅgalyāśca pavitrāśca rakṣoghnā rocanāstathā ..
tāsāṃ śṛṅgodakaṃ viprā jāhnavīsalilopamam .. 5 ..
3.59.d:
मङ्गल्याश्च पवित्राश्च रक्षोघ्ना रोचनास्तथा ॥
तासां शृङ्गोदकं विप्रा जाह्नवीसलिलोपमम् ॥ 5 ॥
3.59.m:
They are auspicious, pure, demon-destroying, and yield yellow pigment;
the water from their horns, O brahmins, is equal to the water of the Gaṅgā.

3.59.s:
gavāṃ kāṇḍūyanānmartyaḥ sarvaṃ pāpaṃ vyapohati ..
tāsāṃ grāsapradānena mahatpuṇyamavāpnuyāt .. 6 ..
3.59.d:
गवां काण्डूयनान्मर्त्यः सर्वं पापं व्यपोहति ॥
तासां ग्रासप्रदानेन महत्पुण्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 6 ॥
3.59.m:
By scratching cows, a mortal dispels all sin;
by giving them a mouthful [of fodder], he attains great religious merit.

3.59.s:
tāsāṃ ca pracaraṃ kṛtvā tathaiva salilāśayam ..
svargalokamupāśnanti bahūnyabdagaṇāni tu .. 7 ..
3.59.d:
तासां च प्रचरं कृत्वा तथैव सलिलाशयम् ॥
स्वर्गलोकमुपाश्नन्ति बहून्यब्दगणानि तु ॥ 7 ॥
3.59.m:
By making a pasture for them, and likewise a pool of water,
they enjoy the world of heaven for many cycles of years.

3.59.s:
tāsāṃ pracārabhūmiṃ tu kṛtvā prāpnoti mānavaḥ ..
aśvamedhasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 8 ..
3.59.d:
तासां प्रचारभूमिं तु कृत्वा प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
अश्वमेधस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोत्यसंशयम् ॥ 8 ॥
3.59.m:
Having created pastureland for them, a man attains,
without doubt, the fruit of the horse sacrifice.

3.59.s:
tāsāmāvasathaṃ kṛtvā nagarādhipatirbhavet ..
tathā lavaṇadānena saubhāgyaṃ mahadaśnute .. 9 ..
3.59.d:
तासामावसथं कृत्वा नगराधिपतिर्भवेत् ॥
तथा लवणदानेन सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥ 9 ॥
3.59.m:
By building a shelter for them, one becomes a ruler of a city;
likewise, by the giving of salt, he obtains great good fortune.

3.59.s:
āturāṃ paṅkalagnāṃ vā coravyāghrabhayārditām ..
mokṣayitvā dvijaśreṣṭhāstvaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet .. 3.291.10 ..
3.59.d:
आतुरां पङ्कलग्नां वा चोरव्याघ्रभयार्दिताम् ॥
मोक्षयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठास्त्वश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ॥ 3.291.10 ॥
3.59.m:
Having rescued [a cow] that is sick, stuck in the mud,
or distressed by fear of thieves or tigers, O best of the twice-born, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice.

3.59.s:
tāsāmauṣadhadānena virogastvabhijāyate ..
vipramocya bhayebhyaśca na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit .. 11 ..
3.59.d:
तासामौषधदानेन विरोगस्त्वभिजायते ॥
विप्रमोच्य भयेभ्यश्च न भयं विद्यते क्वचित् ॥ 11 ॥
3.59.m:
By giving medicine to them, one is born free from disease;
and having freed [them] from dangers, no danger is found for him anywhere.

3.59.s:
krītvā caṇḍālahastācca gomedhasya phalaṃ labhet ..
gopakastvasya cānyasya krītvā hastāttathaiva ca .. 12 ..
3.59.d:
क्रीत्वा चण्डालहस्ताच्च गोमेधस्य फलं लभेत् ॥
गोपकस्त्वस्य चान्यस्य क्रीत्वा हस्तात्तथैव च ॥ 12 ॥
3.59.m:
Having bought [a cow] from the hand of a caṇḍāla, one obtains the fruit of a cow sacrifice;
and likewise [the cowherd] having bought [it] from the hand of another cowherd.

3.59.s:
kṛtvā śītātapatrāṇaṃ tāsāṃ svargamavāpnuyāt ..
utthitāsūtthitastiṣṭhedviṣṭhitāsu ca viṣṭhitaḥ .. 13 ..
3.59.d:
कृत्वा शीतातपत्राणं तासां स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् ॥
उत्थितासूत्थितस्तिष्ठेद्विष्ठितासु च विष्ठितः ॥ 13 ॥
3.59.m:
Having made protection from cold and heat for them, one attains heaven;
when they stand, one should stand, and when they lie down, one should lie down.

3.59.s:
bhuktavatsu tu cāśnīyājjale pīte pibettu ca ..
gomūtreṇācaretsnānaṃ gopurīṣāttathā yavaiḥ .. 14 ..
3.59.d:
भुक्तवत्सु तु चाश्नीयाज्जले पीते पिबेत्तु च ॥
गोमूत्रेणाचरेत्स्नानं गोपुरीषात्तथा यवैः ॥ 14 ॥
3.59.m:
One should eat only when they have eaten, and drink only when water has been drunk [by them];
one should perform bathing with cow urine, and likewise with barley grains [taken] from cow dung.

3.59.s:
śarīrayātrāṃ kurvīta gorasairatha vā dvijāḥ ..
etaddhi govrataṃ māsātsarvakalmaṣanāśanam .. 15 ..
3.59.d:
शरीरयात्रां कुर्वीत गोरसैरथ वा द्विजाः ॥
एतद्धि गोव्रतं मासात्सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥ 15 ॥
3.59.m:
Or, O twice-born, one should maintain one's bodily existence on cow products;
this indeed is the vow of the cow, which destroys all impurities after a month.

3.59.s:
ekāṃ gāṃ dhārayenmāsaṃ dadyāttasyāstathā yavān ..
gomayāttānsamaśnīyānmāsamekamataḥ śuciḥ .. 16 ..
3.59.d:
एकां गां धारयेन्मासं दद्यात्तस्यास्तथा यवान् ॥
गोमयात्तान्समश्नीयान्मासमेकमतः शुचिः ॥ 16 ॥
3.59.m:
One should keep a single cow for a month and give her barley grains;
one should eat those [grains gathered] from cow dung, pure, for one month.

3.59.s:
māsānte tāṃ tathā dhenuṃ dadyādviprāya bhaktimān ..
vratametatsamuddiṣṭaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam . .. 17 ..
3.59.d:
मासान्ते तां तथा धेनुं दद्याद्विप्राय भक्तिमान् ॥
व्रतमेतत्समुद्दिष्टं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥। 17 ॥
3.59.m:
At the end of the month, devoted, he should give that milch cow to a brahmin;
this vow is declared to destroy all sins.

3.59.s:
rājasūyāśvamedhābhyāṃ vratametattathādhikam ..
vratenānena cīrṇena kāmāniṣṭānavāpnuyāt .. 18 ..
3.59.d:
राजसूयाश्वमेधाभ्यां व्रतमेतत्तथाधिकम् ॥
व्रतेनानेन चीर्णेन कामानिष्टानवाप्नुयात् ॥ 18 ॥
3.59.m:
This vow is superior even to the rājasūya and aśvamedha [sacrifices];
by observing this vow, one attains desired wishes.

3.59.s:
vimānenārkavarṇena brahmalokaṃ ca gacchati ..
vināpi gopradānena vratametanmahāphalam..19..
3.59.d:
विमानेनार्कवर्णेन ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ॥
विनापि गोप्रदानेन व्रतमेतन्महाफलम्॥19॥
3.59.m:
He goes to the world of Brahmā in an aerial chariot shining like the sun;
even without giving a cow, this vow yields great fruit.

3.59.s:
trirātraṃ saptarātraṃ vā śaktiṃ jñātvā tathā svakām..
gavāṃ nirhāranirmuktairvṛttiṃ kṛtvā tathā yavaiḥ..3.291.20..
3.59.d:
त्रिरात्रं सप्तरात्रं वा शक्तिं ज्ञात्वा तथा स्वकाम्॥
गवां निर्हारनिर्मुक्तैर्वृत्तिं कृत्वा तथा यवैः॥3.291.20॥
3.59.m:
For three nights or seven nights, knowing one's own capacity,
sustaining oneself on barley grains extracted from the dung of cows,

3.59.s:
pāpamokṣamavāpnoti puṇyaṃ ca mahadaśnute ..
rajaśca gokhurodbhūtaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..21..
3.59.d:
पापमोक्षमवाप्नोति पुण्यं च महदश्नुते ॥
रजश्च गोखुरोद्भूतं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥21॥
3.59.m:
he attains liberation from sin and obtains great religious merit;
and dust raised by the hooves of cows destroys all blemishes.

3.59.s:
yādṛśāttādṛśāddeśānnātra kāryā vicāraṇā ..
maṅgalyaṃ ca pavitraṃ ca tadalakṣmīvināśanam ..22..
3.59.d:
यादृशात्तादृशाद्देशान्नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
मङ्गल्यं च पवित्रं च तदलक्ष्मीविनाशनम् ॥22॥
3.59.m:
From whatever place it comes, no deliberation is to be made here;
it is auspicious, pure, and destroys misfortune.

3.59.s:
gavāṃ hi parivāsena bhūmiḥ śuddhimavāpnuyāt ..
taddhi śuddhaṃ yadā veśma yatra tiṣṭhanti dhenavaḥ ..23..
3.59.d:
गवां हि परिवासेन भूमिः शुद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
तद्धि शुद्धं यदा वेश्म यत्र तिष्ठन्ति धेनवः ॥23॥
3.59.m:
By the abiding of cows, the ground attains purity;
for that dwelling is pure where milch cows abide.

3.59.s:
tāsānniḥśvāsavātena puraṃ nīrājanaṃ bhavet ..
tāsāṃ saṃsparśanaṃ puṇyaṃ duḥsvapnāghavināśanam..24..
3.59.d:
तासान्निःश्वासवातेन पुरं नीराजनं भवेत् ॥
तासां संस्पर्शनं पुण्यं दुःस्वप्नाघविनाशनम्॥24॥
3.59.m:
By the wind of their breath, a city is consecrated with the waving of lights;
touching them is meritorious, destroying evil dreams and sins.

3.59.s:
grīvāmastakasandhau tu tāsāṃ gaṅgā pratiṣṭhitā .
sarvadevamayā gāvaḥ sarva tīrthamayāstathā..25..
3.59.d:
ग्रीवामस्तकसन्धौ तु तासां गङ्गा प्रतिष्ठिता ।
सर्वदेवमया गावः सर्व तीर्थमयास्तथा॥25॥
3.59.m:
The Gaṅgā is established at the junction of their neck and head;
cows consist of all the gods and embody all sacred fords.

3.59.s:
tāsāṃ lomāni puṇyāni pavitrāṇi tathā dvijāḥ ..
gomayenopaliptaṃ tu śuci sthānaṃ prakīrtitam .. 26 ..
3.59.d:
तासां लोमानि पुण्यानि पवित्राणि तथा द्विजाः ॥
गोमयेनोपलिप्तं तु शुचि स्थानं प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 26 ॥
3.59.m:
Their hairs are meritorious and pure, O twice-born;
a place smeared with cow dung is proclaimed to be clean.

3.59.s:
agnyāgārasurāgārāngomayenopalepayet ..
gomaye tu sadā lakṣmīḥ svayameva vyasthitā ..27..
3.59.d:
अग्न्यागारसुरागारान्गोमयेनोपलेपयेत् ॥
गोमये तु सदा लक्ष्मीः स्वयमेव व्यस्थिता ॥27॥
3.59.m:
One should smear fire-sanctuaries and temple shrines with cow dung;
for Lakṣmī herself is ever present in cow dung.

3.59.s:
gomūtre ca tathā gaṅgā dadhikṣīraghṛteṣu ca ..
sadā vyavasthitaṃ somaṃ rocanāyāṃ sarasvatī..28..
3.59.d:
गोमूत्रे च तथा गङ्गा दधिक्षीरघृतेषु च ॥
सदा व्यवस्थितं सोमं रोचनायां सरस्वती॥28॥
3.59.m:
And Gaṅgā is likewise in cow urine; and in curd, milk, and clarified butter
Soma is ever present; Sarasvatī is in [their] yellow pigment.

3.59.s:
viṣṇuryajñaḥ samākhyātaḥ sa ca goṣu pratiṣṭhitaḥ ..
tasmādgāvo vinirdiṣṭā viṣṇureva purātanaiḥ .. 29 ..
3.59.d:
विष्णुर्यज्ञः समाख्यातः स च गोषु प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
तस्माद्गावो विनिर्दिष्टा विष्णुरेव पुरातनैः ॥ 29 ॥
3.59.m:
Viṣṇu is declared to be the sacrifice, and that [sacrifice] is established in cows;
therefore cows are proclaimed to be Viṣṇu himself by the ancients.

3.59.s:
pūjyāstāstu namaskāryāḥ kīrtanīyāśca tāstathā ..
tāsāmāhāradānaṃ ca kāryaṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ tathā..3.291.30..
3.59.d:
पूज्यास्तास्तु नमस्कार्याः कीर्तनीयाश्च तास्तथा ॥
तासामाहारदानं च कार्यं शुश्रूषणं तथा॥3.291.30॥
3.59.m:
They are to be worshipped, saluted with reverence, and praised;
and giving food to them as well as serving them is to be done.

3.59.s:
śuśrūṣaṇeneha gavāṃ dvijendrāḥ prāpnoti lokānamalānviśokān..
tasmātprayatnena gavāṃ hi kāryaṃ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ dharmaparairmanuṣyaiḥ..31..
3.292
haṃsa uvāca ..
yo dayāvānsa puruṣo nirghṛṇo rākṣaso mataḥ ..
rākṣasānāmapi ghṛṇā vidyate dvijasattamāḥ .. ..1..
nirghṛṇāḥ pratipadyante ghoraṃ narakamañjasā ..
vadhabandhaparikleśānmānuṣye'tha labhanti te ..2..
vyādhyārtā duḥkhitā dīnā daridrāśca bhavanti te ..
dayānvitā virājante nākamāsādya mānavāḥ ..3..
tasmāddayāvatā bhāvyaṃ tṛṇeṣvapi vipaścitā ..
tṛṇānyapi sajīvāni teṣāṃ kuryānna pīḍanam .. .. 4 ..
kīṭe pataṅge ca paśau dayā kāryā tathā mṛge ..
varṇottame varṇahīne patite varṇasaṅkare .. 5 ..
sarvatraiva dayā kāryā sarvakāmaphalapradā ..
vratānāmapi sarveṣāṃ śreṣṭhamekaṃ dayāvratam .. 6 ..
3.59.d:
शुश्रूषणेनेह गवां द्विजेन्द्राः प्राप्नोति लोकानमलान्विशोकान्॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन गवां हि कार्यं शुश्रूषणं धर्मपरैर्मनुष्यैः॥31॥
3.292
हंस उवाच ॥
यो दयावान्स पुरुषो निर्घृणो राक्षसो मतः ॥
राक्षसानामपि घृणा विद्यते द्विजसत्तमाः ॥ ॥1॥
निर्घृणाः प्रतिपद्यन्ते घोरं नरकमञ्जसा ॥
वधबन्धपरिक्लेशान्मानुष्येऽथ लभन्ति ते ॥2॥
व्याध्यार्ता दुःखिता दीना दरिद्राश्च भवन्ति ते ॥
दयान्विता विराजन्ते नाकमासाद्य मानवाः ॥3॥
तस्माद्दयावता भाव्यं तृणेष्वपि विपश्चिता ॥
तृणान्यपि सजीवानि तेषां कुर्यान्न पीडनम् ॥ ॥ 4 ॥
कीटे पतङ्गे च पशौ दया कार्या तथा मृगे ॥
वर्णोत्तमे वर्णहीने पतिते वर्णसङ्करे ॥ 5 ॥
सर्वत्रैव दया कार्या सर्वकामफलप्रदा ॥
व्रतानामपि सर्वेषां श्रेष्ठमेकं दयाव्रतम् ॥ 6 ॥

3.59.s:
duḥkhārtaṃ prāṇinaṃ kiñciduḥkhānmokṣayate dvijāḥ ..
vahniṣṭomaphalaṃ proktaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 7 ..
paricaryāṃ tathā kṛtvā sāntvayetprāṇino dvijāḥ..
brahmalokamavāpnoti dayāvāntena karmaṇā .. 8 ..
śleṣmamūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ vyādhitasyājugupsakaḥ ..
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute ..9..
mṛtasya vāpyanāthasya na jugupsanti ye narāḥ ..
kurvanti caiva saṃskārānte narāḥ svargagāminaḥ ..3.292.10..
agnidāhājjalācchastrāttathānyasmādupadravāt ..
prāṇino mokṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā svargaloke mahīyate .. 11 ..
bandhanātprāṇinaḥ kṛtvā mokṣaṇaṃ ca tathā dvijāḥ..
sarvakāmasamṛddhasya yajñasya phalamaśnute..12..
yasmāddhi prāṇinaṃ duḥkhātpuruṣo mokṣayetkvacit..
na tadduḥkhamavāpnoti yatrayatrābhijāyate ..13..
sarvabhūteṣu yo dānaṃ caikasattve ca yā dayā ..
sarvasattvapradānāddhi dayā jñeyā mahāphalā..14..
3.59.d:
दुःखार्तं प्राणिनं किञ्चिदुःखान्मोक्षयते द्विजाः ॥
वह्निष्टोमफलं प्रोक्तं नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 7 ॥
परिचर्यां तथा कृत्वा सान्त्वयेत्प्राणिनो द्विजाः॥
ब्रह्मलोकमवाप्नोति दयावान्तेन कर्मणा ॥ 8 ॥
श्लेष्ममूत्रपुरीषाणां व्याधितस्याजुगुप्सकः ॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते ॥9॥
मृतस्य वाप्यनाथस्य न जुगुप्सन्ति ये नराः ॥
कुर्वन्ति चैव संस्कारान्ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥3.292.10॥
अग्निदाहाज्जलाच्छस्त्रात्तथान्यस्मादुपद्रवात् ॥
प्राणिनो मोक्षणं कृत्वा स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥ 11 ॥
बन्धनात्प्राणिनः कृत्वा मोक्षणं च तथा द्विजाः॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धस्य यज्ञस्य फलमश्नुते॥12॥
यस्माद्धि प्राणिनं दुःखात्पुरुषो मोक्षयेत्क्वचित्॥
न तद्दुःखमवाप्नोति यत्रयत्राभिजायते ॥13॥
सर्वभूतेषु यो दानं चैकसत्त्वे च या दया ॥
सर्वसत्त्वप्रदानाद्धि दया ज्ञेया महाफला॥14॥
3.59.m:
If one releases any living being afflicted with suffering from that suffering, O twice-born,
the fruit of an Agniṣṭoma sacrifice is proclaimed [for him]; no doubt is to be entertained here.
Attending to living beings and comforting them, O twice-born,
the compassionate man attains the world of Brahmā by that deed.
One who feels no revulsion toward the phlegm, urine, and feces of a sick person
obtains the fruit of a sacrifice complete with all desires.
Those men who feel no revulsion toward a deceased or helpless person,
and perform funeral rites, those men go to heaven.
Having rescued a living being from burning by fire, from water, from a weapon,
and from other afflictions, he is honored in the world of heaven.
Likewise, having released a living being from bondage, O twice-born,
one obtains the fruit of a sacrifice complete with all desires.
From whatever suffering a man might release a living being anywhere,
he does not experience that suffering wherever he is born.
Whatever [merit lies in] gift-giving to all beings, and whatever compassion [is shown] to a single living being,
compassion is known to bear greater fruit than the gifting of all beings.

3.59.s:
dayānvitānāṃ tridaśendralokā dayānvitānāṃ ca pitāmahasya ..
dayānvitānāṃ ca samastakāmā lokadvaye vipravarā pradiṣṭāḥ..15..
3.293
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
dākṣiṇyaṃ paramaṃ loke nṛṇāṃ saṃvananaṃ param ..
dākṣiṇyayuktasya tathā pareṣāṃ priyakāritā .. 1 ..
priyāṇyācarate yastu pareṣāṃ manujottamaḥ ..
samāpnoti priyāṇyeva lokayorubhayordvijāḥ .. 2 ..
pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣaṃ ca pareṣāmācaretpriyam ..
priyeṇa vipriyaṃ haṃti priyeṇa priyamāpnuyāt .. 3 ..
mṛdunā dāruṇaṃ hanti mṛdunā haṃti mārdavam ..
sarvaṃ hi mṛdunā hanti tasmāttīkṣṇataro mṛduḥ .. 4 ..
mṛdoriha vadānyasya devā nighnanti śātravān ..
abhicāraḥ sa śatrūṇāṃ narasya mṛdutā tathā ..5..
nareṇa mṛdunā dagdhā mārdavenābhitastu ye ..
na prarohaṃti te viprā bījā dagdhā yathā tathā .. 6 ..
3.59.d:
दयान्वितानां त्रिदशेन्द्रलोका दयान्वितानां च पितामहस्य ॥
दयान्वितानां च समस्तकामा लोकद्वये विप्रवरा प्रदिष्टाः॥15॥
3.293
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
दाक्षिण्यं परमं लोके नृणां संवननं परम् ॥
दाक्षिण्ययुक्तस्य तथा परेषां प्रियकारिता ॥ 1 ॥
प्रियाण्याचरते यस्तु परेषां मनुजोत्तमः ॥
समाप्नोति प्रियाण्येव लोकयोरुभयोर्द्विजाः ॥ 2 ॥
प्रत्यक्षं च परोक्षं च परेषामाचरेत्प्रियम् ॥
प्रियेण विप्रियं हंति प्रियेण प्रियमाप्नुयात् ॥ 3 ॥
मृदुना दारुणं हन्ति मृदुना हंति मार्दवम् ॥
सर्वं हि मृदुना हन्ति तस्मात्तीक्ष्णतरो मृदुः ॥ 4 ॥
मृदोरिह वदान्यस्य देवा निघ्नन्ति शात्रवान् ॥
अभिचारः स शत्रूणां नरस्य मृदुता तथा ॥5॥
नरेण मृदुना दग्धा मार्दवेनाभितस्तु ये ॥
न प्ररोहंति ते विप्रा बीजा दग्धा यथा तथा ॥ 6 ॥
3.59.m:
For those endowed with compassion are the worlds of the lord of the thirty [gods]; and for those endowed with compassion is the world of the Grandfather;
and for those endowed with compassion all desires are ordained in both worlds, O best of brahmins.
3.293
The Haṃsa said:
Courtesy is supreme in the world, the highest means of winning people over; / likewise, for one endowed with courtesy, there is the doing of what is pleasing to others.
The best among men who performs pleasing deeds for others, / attains only pleasing things in both worlds, O twice-born.
In their presence and in their absence, one should act pleasantly toward others; / by what is pleasant one overcomes what is unpleasant, by what is pleasant one attains what is pleasant.
With the gentle, one destroys the harsh; with the gentle, one destroys gentleness; / indeed, one overcomes everything with the gentle; therefore, the gentle is sharper [than the harsh].
The gods destroy the enemies of a gentle, generous person in this world; / thus a man's gentleness is itself an incantation against his enemies.
Those who are completely burned by a gentle man by means of his gentleness, / do not sprout again, O twice-born, just like burned seeds.

3.59.s:
dākṣiṇyamekaṃ subhagatvaheturdākṣiṇyamekaṃ tridivasya hetuḥ ..
dākṣiṇyamāsthāya jayedarātīndākṣiṇyayuktastu sadā bhavecca..7..
3.294
.. haṃsa uvāca .. ..
saṃrohatīṣuṇāviddhaṃ vanaṃ paraśunā hatam ..
vācā duruktaṃ bībhatsaṃ na saṃrohati vākkṛtam .. 1 ..
mitrāṇi yāṃti śatrutvaṃ narasyāpriyavādinaḥ ..
anarthāḥ svayamāyāṃti mṛto narakamṛcchati .. 2 ..
tasmādbhāvyaṃ manuṣyeṇa smitapūrvābhibhāṣiṇā ..
pratyakṣaṃ ca parokṣaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ priyabhāṣiṇām .. 3 ..
mitratāṃ yāṃti ripavo narāṇāṃ priyabhāṣiṇām ..
rakṣāṃsyapi nigṛhyante puruṣaiḥ sāntvavādibhiḥ .. 4 ..
priyavākyātparaṃ loke nāsti saṃvananaṃ param ..
priyo bhavati lokānāṃ priyavādī tathā naraḥ .. 5 ..
priyaṃvadānāṃ sakalaṃ jagadetatsthitaṃ vaśe ..
priyaṃvadānāṃ śatrutve nāsti kaścijjagattraye .. 6 ..
3.59.d:
दाक्षिण्यमेकं सुभगत्वहेतुर्दाक्षिण्यमेकं त्रिदिवस्य हेतुः ॥
दाक्षिण्यमास्थाय जयेदरातीन्दाक्षिण्ययुक्तस्तु सदा भवेच्च॥7॥
3.294
॥ हंस उवाच ॥ ॥
संरोहतीषुणाविद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् ॥
वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्कृतम् ॥ 1 ॥
मित्राणि यांति शत्रुत्वं नरस्याप्रियवादिनः ॥
अनर्थाः स्वयमायांति मृतो नरकमृच्छति ॥ 2 ॥
तस्माद्भाव्यं मनुष्येण स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिणा ॥
प्रत्यक्षं च परोक्षं च सर्वेषां प्रियभाषिणाम् ॥ 3 ॥
मित्रतां यांति रिपवो नराणां प्रियभाषिणाम् ॥
रक्षांस्यपि निगृह्यन्ते पुरुषैः सान्त्ववादिभिः ॥ 4 ॥
प्रियवाक्यात्परं लोके नास्ति संवननं परम् ॥
प्रियो भवति लोकानां प्रियवादी तथा नरः ॥ 5 ॥
प्रियंवदानां सकलं जगदेतत्स्थितं वशे ॥
प्रियंवदानां शत्रुत्वे नास्ति कश्चिज्जगत्त्रये ॥ 6 ॥
3.59.m:
Courtesy alone is the cause of good fortune; courtesy alone is the cause of heaven; / having resorted to courtesy, one may conquer enemies; one should always be endowed with courtesy.
3.294
The Haṃsa said:
[A body] pierced by an arrow heals; a forest struck down by an axe grows back; / but what is ill-spoken, repulsive, caused by speech, does not heal.
Friends become enemies for a man who speaks unpleasant words; / misfortunes arrive of their own accord, and upon dying he goes to hell.
Therefore, a person should be one who speaks preceded by a smile, / speaking pleasantly to all, both in their presence and in their absence.
Enemies turn into friends for men who speak pleasantly; / even demons are brought under control by men who speak soothing words.
In this world, there is no higher means of winning others over than pleasant speech; / a man who speaks pleasantly becomes dear to people.
This entire world remains under the control of those who speak kindly; / for those who speak kindly, there is no one who remains an enemy in the three worlds.

3.59.s:
priyaṃvadāḥ saukhyamihāpnuvaṃti priyaṃvadā nākamatha prayāṃti ..
priyaṃvadāḥ sarvamathāpnuvaṃti priyaṃvadaḥ syādata eva nityam ..7..

alasānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ prāptopyartho vinaśyati ..2..

3.59.d:
प्रियंवदाः सौख्यमिहाप्नुवंति प्रियंवदा नाकमथ प्रयांति ॥
प्रियंवदाः सर्वमथाप्नुवंति प्रियंवदः स्यादत एव नित्यम् ॥7॥
3.295
॥ हंस उवाच ॥
अलसानां मनुष्याणां सदा दुःखं दरिद्रता ॥
आलस्यं पातकं लोके आलस्यं भूतिनाशनम् ॥ 1 ॥
नाधिगच्छन्ति भोक्तव्यमलसा ये नराधमाः ॥
अलसानां मनुष्याणां प्राप्तोप्यर्थो विनश्यति ॥2॥
तस्मान्नित्यं मनुष्येण दाक्ष्यं कार्यं विजानता ॥
दक्षः सर्वमवाप्नोति यत्किञ्चिन्मनसेच्छति ॥ 3 ॥
धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च मोक्षे च द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
भाजनं सर्वकालेषु दक्ष एव सदा नरः॥॥
आकृष्य दक्षः केशेषु विमुखामपि च श्रियम् ॥
स्वीकरोति महाभागा दक्षे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ 5 ॥
उत्थानधीरः पुरुषो वाग्वीरानधितिष्ठति ॥
उत्थानधीरं वाग्धीरा रमयन्त उपासते ॥ 6 ॥
3.59.m:
Those who speak kindly attain happiness here; those who speak kindly go to heaven; / those who speak kindly attain everything; therefore, one should always be a speaker of kind words.
3.295
The Haṃsa said:
For lazy men, there is always misery and poverty; / laziness is a sin in this world; laziness is the destruction of prosperity.
Those base men who are lazy do not obtain food to eat; / for lazy men, even wealth that has been acquired perishes.
Therefore, a discerning man must always practice diligence; / a diligent person attains everything, whatever he desires in his mind.
In dharma, in wealth, in desire, and in liberation, O best of the twice-born, / only the diligent man is ever the proper vessel at all times. / Having pulled Fortune by the hair, even when she has turned away, / the diligent man takes possession of her, O fortunate ones; everything is established in the diligent.
A man resolute in exertion surpasses those who are merely heroes in speech; / those resolute in speech attend upon the man resolute in exertion, bringing him delight.

3.59.s:
utthānavāneva divaṃ prayāti utthānavāneva paraṃ padañca ..
utthānavāneva naro jayī syāttasmātsadotthānapareṇa bhāvyam .. 7 ..
3.59.d:
उत्थानवानेव दिवं प्रयाति उत्थानवानेव परं पदञ्च ॥
उत्थानवानेव नरो जयी स्यात्तस्मात्सदोत्थानपरेण भाव्यम् ॥ 7 ॥
3.59.m: Only one endowed with exertion goes to heaven, and only one endowed with exertion goes to the supreme abode; / only a man endowed with exertion is victorious; therefore, one should always be devoted to exertion.
